simetri.geom.nonlinear.path

Path builders for polylines, Beziers, arcs, and related operations.

Path2D (alias LinPath) is a Group that accumulates drawing operations from a turtle-like pen state.

Examples

import simetri.graphics as sg
p = sg.Path2D(start=(0, 0), angle=0)
_ = p.line_to((10, 0)).turn(sg.pi / 2).forward(10).close()

 117def _xy_point(point: PointType) -> tuple[float, float]:
 118    """Return ``(x, y)`` as floats from a 2- or 3-vector."""
 119    x, y = point[:2]
 120    return (float(x), float(y))
 121
 122
 123def _polyline_point_at_length(
 124    vertices: Sequence[PointType], target_length: float
 125) -> tuple[float, float]:
 126    """Return the point at arc length ``target_length`` along a polyline."""
 127    if target_length <= 0:
 128        return _xy_point(vertices[0])
 129    remaining = target_length
 130    for index in range(len(vertices) - 1):
 131        start = vertices[index]
 132        end = vertices[index + 1]
 133        edge_length = distance(start, end)
 134        if remaining <= edge_length:
 135            if edge_length == 0:
 136                return _xy_point(start)
 137            return _xy_point(lerp_point(start, end, remaining / edge_length))
 138        remaining -= edge_length
 139    return _xy_point(vertices[-1])

 168class Path2D(Group, CommonStyle):
 169    """Constructive 2D path with a pen position and heading.
 170
 171    Operations such as ``line_to``, ``cubic_to``, and ``arc`` append geometry
 172    while updating ``pos`` and ``angle``. The path is also a ``Group`` of
 173    ``Shape`` segments for transforms and drawing.
 174
 175    ``color`` sets both ``line_color`` and ``fill_color``. ``alpha`` sets both
 176    ``line_alpha`` and ``fill_alpha``. Reading an unset ``line_color`` /
 177    ``fill_color`` / ``line_alpha`` / ``fill_alpha`` returns the matching
 178    configured default. Style color/alpha and ``copy_style`` come from
 179    ``CommonStyle``.
 180
 181    Attributes:
 182        pos: Current pen position.
 183        start: Path start point.
 184        angle: Current heading in radians.
 185        operations: List of ``Operation`` records.
 186        subtype: ``Types.PATH2D``.
 187
 188    Examples:
 189        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 190        >>> path = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=0)
 191        >>> _ = path.forward(40).turn(sg.pi / 2).forward(20)
 192        >>> round(path.pos[0], 6), round(path.pos[1], 6)
 193        (40.0, 20.0)
 194"""
 195
 196    # Group.__setattr__ adds a frame above the color/alpha property setters.
 197    _style_warning_stacklevel: int = 4
 198

 239            start: Starting pen position. Defaults to ``(0, 0)``.

 347    def __str__(self) -> str:

 353        Examples:
 354            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 355            >>> str(sg.Path2D()).startswith("Path2D")
 356            True

 358        if self.elements is None or len(self.elements) == 0:
 359            res = "Path2D()"
 360        elif len(self.elements) in [1, 2]:

 362        else:

 379    def _create_object(self) -> None:
 380        """Build geometry for the most recently appended operation."""
 381        PO = PathOps
 382        op = self.operations[-1]
 383        op_type = op.subtype
 384        data = op.data
 385        if op_type in _OPEN_SUBPATH_OPS and self.cur_shape.closed:
 386            self.cur_shape = Shape([self.pos])
 387            self.append(self.cur_shape)
 388        if op_type in _MOVE_PATH_OPS:
 389            self.cur_shape = Shape([data])
 390            self.append(self.cur_shape)
 391            self.objects.append(None)
 392        elif op_type in _LINE_PATH_OPS:
 393            self.objects.append(Shape(data))
 394            self.cur_shape.append(data[1])
 395        elif op_type == PO.SEGMENTS:
 396            self.objects.append(Shape(data[1]))
 397            self.cur_shape.extend(data[1])
 398        elif op_type in _SINE_PATH_OPS:
 399            self.objects.append(Shape(data[0]))
 400            self.cur_shape.extend(data[0])
 401        elif op_type in _BEZIER_PATH_OPS:
 402            n_points = runtime_defaults["n_bezier_points"]
 403            curve = Bezier(data, n_points=n_points)
 404            self.objects.append(curve)
 405            self.cur_shape.extend(curve.vertices[1:])
 406            if op_type == PO.CUBIC_TO:
 407                self.handles.extend([(data[0], data[1]), (data[2], data[3])])
 408            else:
 409                self.handles.append((data[0], data[1]))
 410                self.handles.append((data[1], data[2]))
 411        elif op_type == PO.HOBBY_TO:
 412            n_points = runtime_defaults["n_hobby_points"]
 413            start = data[0]
 414            through = list(data[1])
 415            if through and close_points_square(start, through[0]):
 416                through = through[1:]
 417            curve = hobby_shape([start, *through], n_points=n_points)
 418            self.objects.append(Shape(curve.vertices))
 419            self.cur_shape.extend(curve.vertices[1:])
 420        elif op_type in _ARC_PATH_OPS:
 421            self.objects.append(Shape(data[-1]))
 422            self.cur_shape.extend(data[-1][1:])
 423        elif op_type == PO.CLOSE:
 424            self.cur_shape.closed = True
 425            self.objects.append(None)
 426        else:
 427            raise ValueError(f"Invalid operation type: {op_type}")
 428
 429    def copy(self) -> "Path2D":
 430        """Return a deep-enough copy of the path for independent editing.
 431
 432        Returns:
 433            Path2D: Copied path with cloned elements and operations.
 434
 435        Examples:
 436            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 437            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 0))
 438            >>> q = p.copy()
 439            >>> _ = q.line_to((40, 20))
 440            >>> len(p.operations), len(q.operations)
 441            (1, 2)
 442"""
 443
 444        new_path = Path2D(start=self.start)
 445        cur_shape_index = None
 446        for index, element in enumerate(self.elements):
 447            if element is self.cur_shape:
 448                cur_shape_index = index
 449                break
 450
 451        new_path.pos = self.pos
 452        new_path.angle = self.angle
 453        new_path.operations = (
 454            self.operations.copy()
 455        )  # shallow-copy of list is fine if Operations are treated as immutable
 456        new_path.elements = [element.copy() for element in self.elements]
 457        new_path.objects = []
 458        for obj in self.objects:
 459            if obj is not None:
 460                new_path.objects.append(obj.copy())
 461            else:
 462                new_path.objects.append(None)
 463        new_path.even_odd = self.even_odd
 464        new_path.closed = self.closed
 465        if cur_shape_index is not None:
 466            new_path.cur_shape = new_path.elements[cur_shape_index]
 467        else:
 468            new_path.cur_shape = self.cur_shape.copy()
 469        new_path.handles = list(self.handles)
 470        new_path.stack = deque(self.stack)
 471        new_path.copy_style(self)
 472        return new_path
 473
 474    def _add(
 475        self,
 476        pos: PointType,
 477        op: PathOps,
 478        data: object,
 479        pnt2: PointType | None = None,
 480        **kwargs: object,
 481    ) -> None:
 482        """Add an operation and update pen state.
 483
 484        Args:
 485            pos: New pen position after the operation.
 486            op: Path operation kind.
 487            data: Operation payload.
 488            pnt2: Optional point used to update heading. Defaults to None.
 489            **kwargs: ``name`` labels the operation. Other keys are style
 490                overrides applied to the segment.
 491        """
 492        self.operations.append(Operation(op, data))
 493        if op in _HEADING_FROM_DATA_OPS:
 494            self.angle = data[1]
 495        else:
 496            if pnt2 is not None:
 497                self.angle = line_angle(pnt2, pos)
 498            else:
 499                self.angle = line_angle(self.pos, pos)
 500        self._create_object()
 501        style = dict(kwargs)
 502        if "name" in style:
 503            setattr(self, style["name"], self.operations[-1])
 504            del style["name"]
 505        targets = []
 506        segment = self.objects[-1]
 507        if segment is not None:
 508            targets.append(segment)
 509        if self.cur_shape is not None and self.cur_shape is not segment:
 510            targets.append(self.cur_shape)
 511        for target in targets:
 512            for key, value in style.items():
 513                setattr(target, key, value)
 514        list(pos)[:2]
 515        self.pos = pos
 516
 517    @property
 518    def all_vertices(self) -> list:
 519        """Return all vertices of the path after applying transforms.
 520
 521        Returns:
 522            list: Flattened vertex list.
 523
 524        Examples:
 525            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 526            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 0)).line_to((40, 20))
 527            >>> [[round(c, 6) for c in q[:2]] for q in p.all_vertices]
 528            [[0.0, 0.0], [40.0, 0.0], [40.0, 0.0], [40.0, 20.0]]
 529"""
 530        all_vertices = []
 531        for obj in self.objects:
 532            if obj is not None:
 533                all_vertices.extend(obj.vertices)
 534
 535        return all_vertices
 536
 537    @property
 538    def all_elements(self) -> list:
 539        """Return the transformed geometric objects that make up the path.
 540
 541        Returns:
 542            list: Drawable elements in the path group.
 543
 544        Examples:
 545            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 546            >>> path = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 0))
 547            >>> [[round(float(c), 6) or 0.0 for c in q[:2]] for q in path.all_elements[0].vertices]
 548            [[0.0, 0.0], [40.0, 0.0]]
 549        """
 550        return [obj for obj in self.objects if obj is not None]
 551
 552    @property
 553    def sections(self) -> list:
 554        """Geometric sections of the path (alias of ``all_elements``).
 555
 556        Each drawing operation that produces geometry is one section
 557        (``line_to``, ``cubic_to``, ``arc``, …). ``move_to`` and ``close``
 558        do not create sections.
 559
 560        Returns:
 561            list: The same objects as ``all_elements``.
 562
 563        Examples:
 564            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 565            >>> path = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 0)).line_to((40, 20))
 566            >>> len(path.sections)
 567            2
 568            >>> path.sections[0] is path.all_elements[0]
 569            True
 570        """
 571        return self.all_elements

 573    def uniform_points(
 574        self,
 575        distance: float,
 576        align_section_ends: bool = True,
 577        align_path_end: bool = True,
 578        rel_tol: float | None = None,
 579        abs_tol: float | None = None,
 580    ) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
 581        """Return points spaced by ``distance`` along the path.
 582
 583        Sampling restarts on each section. A section end is included when
 584        the leftover stub is within tolerance of ``distance`` (or of 0),
 585        or when the matching align flag is True. On the last section,
 586        ``align_path_end`` is used instead of ``align_section_ends``.
 587        Connected section starts are not repeated; a new subpath start is.
 588
 589        Args:
 590            distance: Arc-length spacing. Must be positive.
 591            align_section_ends: If True, always include each non-final
 592                section end. Defaults to True.
 593            align_path_end: If True, always include the path end.
 594                Defaults to True.
 595            rel_tol: Relative leftover tolerance. ``None`` uses
 596                ``runtime_defaults["rel_tol"]``.
 597            abs_tol: Absolute leftover tolerance. ``None`` uses
 598                ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
 599
 600        Returns:
 601            list[tuple[float, float]]: Sample points in path order.
 602
 603        Raises:
 604            ValueError: If ``distance`` is not positive.
 605
 606        Examples:
 607            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 608            >>> path = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 0))
 609            >>> path.uniform_points(20)
 610            [(0.0, 0.0), (20.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0)]
 611            >>> path.uniform_points(20, align_path_end=False)
 612            [(0.0, 0.0), (20.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0)]
 613            >>> corner = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 0)).line_to((40, 20))
 614            >>> corner.uniform_points(20)
 615            [(0.0, 0.0), (20.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 20.0)]
 616            >>> corner.uniform_points(20, align_section_ends=False)
 617            [(0.0, 0.0), (20.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 20.0)]
 618            >>> path.uniform_points(20, True, True, 0, 0.001)[-1]
 619            (40.0, 0.0)
 620            >>> path.uniform_points(0)
 621            Traceback (most recent call last):
 622                ...
 623            ValueError: distance must be positive
 624        """
 625        if distance <= 0:
 626            raise ValueError("distance must be positive")
 627        rel_tol, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
 628        abs_tol2 = abs_tol * abs_tol
 629
 630        def lengths_close(first: float, second: float) -> bool:
 631            return bool(
 632                np.isclose(first, second, rtol=rel_tol, atol=abs_tol)
 633            )
 634
 635        def append_unique(
 636            points: list[tuple[float, float]], point: PointType
 637        ) -> None:
 638            xy = _xy_point(point)
 639            if points and close_points_square(points[-1], xy, abs_tol2):
 640                return
 641            points.append(xy)
 642
 643        points: list[tuple[float, float]] = []
 644        previous_end: tuple[float, float] | None = None
 645        sections = self.sections
 646        last_index = len(sections) - 1
 647        for index, section in enumerate(sections):
 648            vertices = list(section.vertices)
 649            if not vertices:
 650                continue
 651            start = _xy_point(vertices[0])
 652            end = _xy_point(vertices[-1])
 653            connected = previous_end is not None and close_points_square(
 654                previous_end, start, abs_tol2
 655            )
 656            if not connected:
 657                append_unique(points, start)
 658            if len(vertices) < 2:
 659                previous_end = end
 660                continue
 661            section_length = polyline_length(
 662                vertices, closed=False, abs_tol=abs_tol
 663            )
 664            last_s = 0.0
 665            while True:
 666                next_s = last_s + distance
 667                if next_s > section_length or lengths_close(
 668                    next_s, section_length
 669                ):
 670                    break
 671                append_unique(
 672                    points, _polyline_point_at_length(vertices, next_s)
 673                )
 674                last_s = next_s
 675            leftover = section_length - last_s
 676            align_end = (
 677                align_path_end if index == last_index else align_section_ends
 678            )
 679            if lengths_close(leftover, 0.0):
 680                pass
 681            elif lengths_close(leftover, distance) or align_end:
 682                append_unique(points, end)
 683            previous_end = end
 684        return points
 685
 686    @property
 687    def b_box(self) -> BoundingBox:
 688        """Return the axis-aligned bounding box of the path.
 689
 690        Returns:
 691            Bounding box of all path vertices.
 692
 693        Examples:
 694            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 695            >>> box = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 20)).b_box
 696            >>> box.width, box.height
 697            (40.0, 20.0)
 698"""
 699
 700        return bounding_box(self.all_vertices)
 701
 702    def push(self) -> None:
 703        """Push the current pen position and heading onto the stack.
 704
 705        Examples:
 706            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 707            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=0)
 708            >>> p.push()
 709            >>> _ = p.forward(40)
 710            >>> p.pop()
 711            >>> p.pos
 712            (0, 0)
 713"""
 714        self.stack.append((self.pos, self.angle))
 715
 716    def pop(self) -> None:
 717        """Restore the pen position and heading from the stack.
 718
 719        Starts a new subpath at the restored position so later drawing is
 720        not connected to the segment that was drawn after ``push``. Does
 721        nothing if the stack is empty.
 722
 723        Examples:
 724            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 725            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=0)
 726            >>> p.push()
 727            >>> _ = p.forward(20).turn(sg.pi / 2)
 728            >>> p.pop()
 729            >>> p.angle
 730            0
 731            >>> p.pos
 732            (0, 0)
 733"""
 734        if not self.stack:
 735            return
 736        pos, angle = self.stack.pop()
 737        self.operations.append(Operation(PathOps.MOVE_TO, pos))
 738        self._create_object()
 739        self.pos = pos
 740        self.angle = angle
 741
 742    def r_coord(self, dx: float, dy: float) -> PointType:
 743        """Map local offsets into world coordinates relative to the pen.
 744
 745        The local y-axis is aligned with the current heading.
 746
 747        Args:
 748            dx: Offset along the local x-axis.
 749            dy: Offset along the local y-axis (heading direction).
 750
 751        Returns:
 752            PointType: Absolute point.
 753
 754        Examples:
 755            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 756            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=sg.pi / 2)
 757            >>> x, y = p.r_coord(0, 40)
 758            >>> round(x, 6), round(y, 6)
 759            (0.0, 40.0)
 760"""
 761        x, y = self.pos[:2]
 762        theta = self.angle - pi / 2
 763        x1 = dx * cos(theta) - dy * sin(theta) + x
 764        y1 = dx * sin(theta) + dy * cos(theta) + y
 765
 766        return x1, y1
 767
 768    def r_polar(self, r: float, angle: float) -> PointType:
 769        """Return an absolute point from polar offsets relative to the pen.
 770
 771        Angle ``0`` is aligned with the current heading.
 772
 773        Args:
 774            r: Radius.
 775            angle: Angle in radians relative to the heading.
 776
 777        Returns:
 778            PointType: Absolute point.
 779
 780        Examples:
 781            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 782            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=sg.pi / 2)
 783            >>> x, y = p.r_polar(40, 0)
 784            >>> round(x, 6), round(y, 6)
 785            (40.0, 0.0)
 786"""
 787        x, y = polar_to_cartesian(r, angle + self.angle - pi / 2)[:2]
 788        x1, y1 = self.pos[:2]
 789
 790        return x1 + x, y1 + y
 791
 792    def line_to(self, point: PointType, **kwargs: object) -> Self:
 793        """Draw a straight segment from the current position to ``point``.
 794
 795        Args:
 796            point: Absolute end point.
 797            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
 798
 799        Returns:
 800            Self: This path (for chaining).
 801
 802        Examples:
 803            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 804            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 0))
 805            >>> p.pos
 806            (40, 0)
 807"""
 808        self._add(point, PathOps.LINE_TO, (self.pos, point), **kwargs)
 809
 810        return self
 811
 812    def forward(self, length: float, **kwargs: object) -> Self:
 813        """Advance the pen ``length`` units along the current heading.
 814
 815        Args:
 816            length: Distance to travel.
 817            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
 818
 819        Returns:
 820            Self: This path (for chaining).
 821
 822        Examples:
 823            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 824            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=0).forward(40)
 825            >>> p.pos
 826            (40.0, 0.0)
 827"""
 828
 829        x, y = line_by_point_angle_length(self.pos, self.angle, length)[1][:2]
 830        self._add((x, y), PathOps.FORWARD, (self.pos, (x, y)), **kwargs)
 831
 832        return self
 833
 834    def orient(self, angle: float) -> Self:
 835        """Set the absolute heading angle.
 836
 837        Args:
 838            angle: New heading in radians.
 839
 840        Returns:
 841            Self: This path.
 842
 843        Examples:
 844            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 845            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).orient(sg.pi)
 846            >>> p.angle == sg.pi
 847            True
 848"""
 849        self.angle = angle
 850
 851        return self
 852
 853    def turn(self, angle: float, distance: float = 0) -> Self:
 854        """Turn by ``angle`` radians, optionally moving ``distance`` forward.
 855
 856        Args:
 857            angle: Heading increment in radians.
 858            distance: Optional forward distance after the turn. Defaults to 0.
 859
 860        Returns:
 861            Self: This path.
 862
 863        Examples:
 864            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 865            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=0).turn(sg.pi / 2, distance=40)
 866            >>> round(p.pos[0], 6), round(p.pos[1], 6)
 867            (0.0, 40.0)
 868"""
 869
 870        self.angle += angle
 871        if distance != 0:
 872            self.forward(distance)
 873
 874        return self

 876    def move(
 877        self,
 878        pos: PointType,
 879        anchor: Anchor = Anchor.CENTER,
 880        **kwargs: object,
 881    ) -> Self:
 882        """Translate the whole path so a bbox anchor sits at ``pos``.
 883
 884        Args:
 885            pos: Target location for the chosen anchor.
 886            anchor: Bounding-box anchor (default ``Anchor.CENTER``).
 887            **kwargs: Extra attributes set on the path before transforming.
 888
 889        Returns:
 890            Self or Group: Transformed path (or group when repetitions apply).
 891
 892        Examples:
 893            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 894            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 0))
 895            >>> _ = p.move((50, 50))
 896            >>> abs(p.b_box.center[0] - 50) < 1e-6
 897            True
 898"""
 899        x, y = pos[:2]
 900        anchor = get_enum_value(Anchor, anchor)
 901        x1, y1 = getattr(self.b_box, anchor)
 902        transform = translation_matrix(x - x1, y - y1)
 903        for k, v in kwargs.items():
 904            setattr(self, k, v)
 905        res = self._update(transform, reps=0)
 906
 907        return res
 908
 909    def move_to(self, point: PointType, **kwargs: object) -> Self:
 910        """Lift the pen and start a new subpath at ``point``.
 911
 912        Args:
 913            point: Absolute destination.
 914            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
 915
 916        Returns:
 917            Self: This path.
 918
 919        Examples:
 920            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 921            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((20, 0)).move_to((0, 20))
 922            >>> p.pos
 923            (0, 20)
 924"""
 925        self._add(point, PathOps.MOVE_TO, point)
 926
 927        return self

 929    def r_line(self, dx: float, dy: float, **kwargs: object) -> Self:
 930        """Draw a line using relative offsets from the current position.
 931
 932        Args:
 933            dx: X offset.
 934            dy: Y offset.
 935            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
 936
 937        Returns:
 938            Self: This path.
 939
 940        Examples:
 941            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 942            >>> p = sg.Path2D((40, 40)).r_line(60, 80)
 943            >>> p.pos
 944            (100, 120)
 945"""
 946        point = self.pos[0] + dx, self.pos[1] + dy
 947        self._add(point, PathOps.R_LINE, (self.pos, point), **kwargs)
 948
 949        return self
 950
 951    def r_move(self, dx: float = 0, dy: float = 0, **kwargs: object) -> Self:
 952        """Move the pen by relative offsets without drawing.
 953
 954        Args:
 955            dx: X offset. Defaults to 0.
 956            dy: Y offset. Defaults to 0.
 957            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
 958
 959        Returns:
 960            Self: This path.
 961
 962        Examples:
 963            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 964            >>> p = sg.Path2D((40, 40)).r_move(80, 60)
 965            >>> p.pos
 966            (120, 100)
 967"""
 968        x, y = self.pos[:2]
 969        point = (x + dx, y + dy)
 970        self._add(point, PathOps.R_MOVE, point, **kwargs)
 971        return self

 973    def h_line_to(self, x: float, **kwargs: object) -> Self:
 974        """Draw a horizontal line to absolute x, keeping the current y.
 975
 976        Args:
 977            x: Absolute x coordinate of the end point.
 978            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
 979
 980        Returns:
 981            Self: This path.
 982
 983        Examples:
 984            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 985            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 80)).h_line_to(80)
 986            >>> p.pos
 987            (80, 80)
 988"""
 989        y = self.pos[1]
 990        self._add((x, y), PathOps.H_LINE_TO, (self.pos, (x, y)), **kwargs)
 991        return self

 993    def r_h_line(self, length: float, **kwargs: object) -> Self:
 994        """Draw a horizontal line of the given length.
 995
 996        Args:
 997            length: Signed horizontal distance.
 998            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
 999
1000        Returns:
1001            Self: This path.
1002
1003        Examples:
1004            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1005            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).r_h_line(40)
1006            >>> p.pos
1007            (40, 0)
1008"""
1009        x, y = self.pos[0] + length, self.pos[1]
1010        self._add((x, y), PathOps.R_H_LINE, (self.pos, (x, y)), **kwargs)
1011        return self
1012
1013    def v_line_to(self, y: float, **kwargs: object) -> Self:
1014        """Draw a vertical line to absolute y, keeping the current x.
1015
1016        Args:
1017            y: Absolute y coordinate of the end point.
1018            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1019
1020        Returns:
1021            Self: This path.
1022
1023        Examples:
1024            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1025            >>> p = sg.Path2D((60, 0)).v_line_to(80)
1026            >>> p.pos
1027            (60, 80)
1028"""
1029        x = self.pos[0]
1030        self._add((x, y), PathOps.V_LINE_TO, (self.pos, (x, y)), **kwargs)
1031        return self

1033    def r_v_line(self, length: float, **kwargs: object) -> Self:
1034        """Draw a vertical line of the given length.
1035
1036        Args:
1037            length: Signed vertical distance.
1038            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1039
1040        Returns:
1041            Self: This path.
1042
1043        Examples:
1044            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1045            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).r_v_line(40)
1046            >>> p.pos
1047            (0, 40)
1048"""

1050        self._add((x, y), PathOps.R_V_LINE, (self.pos, (x, y)), **kwargs)

1053    def segments(
1054        self, points: Sequence[PointType], **kwargs: object
1055    ) -> Self:
1056        """Append polyline segments through absolute ``points``.
1057
1058        Args:
1059            points: Sequence of absolute points.
1060            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1061
1062        Returns:
1063            Self: This path.
1064
1065        Examples:
1066            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1067            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).segments([(20, 0), (20, 20)])
1068            >>> p.pos
1069            (20, 20)
1070"""
1071
1072        self._add(
1073            points[-1],
1074            PathOps.SEGMENTS,
1075            (self.pos, points),
1076            pnt2=points[-2],
1077            **kwargs,
1078        )
1079        return self
