class Path2D(simetri.group.batch.Group, simetri.base.common_style.CommonStyle): 
 169class Path2D(Group, CommonStyle):
 170    """Constructive 2D path with a pen position and heading.
 171
 172    Operations such as ``line_to``, ``cubic_to``, and ``arc`` append geometry
 173    while updating ``pos`` and ``angle``. The path is also a ``Group`` of
 174    ``Shape`` segments for transforms and drawing.
 175
 176    ``color`` sets both ``line_color`` and ``fill_color``. ``alpha`` sets both
 177    ``line_alpha`` and ``fill_alpha``. Reading an unset ``line_color`` /
 178    ``fill_color`` / ``line_alpha`` / ``fill_alpha`` returns the matching
 179    configured default. Style color/alpha and ``copy_style`` come from
 180    ``CommonStyle``.
 181
 182    Attributes:
 183        pos: Current pen position.
 184        start: Path start point.
 185        angle: Current heading in radians.
 186        operations: List of ``Operation`` records.
 187        subtype: ``Types.PATH2D``.
 188
 189    Examples:
 190        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 191        >>> path = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=0)
 192        >>> _ = path.forward(40).turn(sg.pi / 2).forward(20)
 193        >>> round(path.pos[0], 6), round(path.pos[1], 6)
 194        (40.0, 20.0)
 195"""
 196
 197    # Group.__setattr__ adds a frame above the color/alpha property setters.
 198    _style_warning_stacklevel: int = 4
 199
 200    def __init__(
 201        self,
 202        start: PointType = (0, 0),
 203        angle: float = pi / 2,
 204        fill: bool = True,
 205        stroke: bool = True,
 206        alpha: float | None = None,
 207        color: Color | None = None,
 208        draw_double: bool = False,
 209        draw_fillets: bool = False,
 210        draw_markers: bool = False,
 211        even_odd: bool | None = None,
 212        back_style: object = None,
 213        double_distance: float | None = None,
 214        double_color: Color | None = None,
 215        fill_alpha: float | None = None,
 216        fill_color: Color | None = None,
 217        fill_mode: FillMode = FillMode.NONZERO,
 218        fillet_radius: float | None = None,
 219        gradient: object = None,
 220        line_alpha: float | None = None,
 221        line_cap: LineCap = LineCap.BUTT,
 222        line_color: Color | None = None,
 223        line_dash_array: object = None,
 224        line_dash_phase: float | None = None,
 225        line_join: LineJoin = LineJoin.MITER,
 226        line_miter_limit: float | None = None,
 227        line_width: float | None = None,
 228        marker_alpha: float | None = None,
 229        marker_color: Color | None = None,
 230        marker_radius: float | None = None,
 231        marker_shape: object = None,
 232        marker_size: float | None = None,
 233        marker_type: object = None,
 234        markers_only: bool | None = None,
 235        smooth: bool | None = None,
 236    ) -> None:
 237        """Initialize a Path2D.
 238
 239        Args:
 240            start: Starting pen position. Defaults to ``(0, 0)``.
 241            angle: Initial heading in radians. Defaults to upward (``pi/2``).
 242            fill: Whether to fill when drawn. Defaults to True.
 243            stroke: Whether to stroke when drawn. Defaults to True.
 244            alpha: Overall opacity override.
 245            color: Convenience color applied to stroke/fill when set.
 246            draw_double: Draw a double stroke if True.
 247            draw_fillets: Draw fillets at corners if True.
 248            draw_markers: Draw markers along the path if True.
 249            even_odd: If True, use even-odd fill rule; ``None`` uses
 250                ``runtime_defaults["even_odd"]`` at draw time.
 251            back_style: Background style.
 252            double_distance: Spacing for double stroke.
 253            double_color: Color for the second stroke.
 254            fill_alpha: Fill opacity. Unset values use ``runtime_defaults['fill_alpha']``.
 255            fill_color: Fill color. Unset values use ``runtime_defaults['fill_color']``.
 256            fill_mode: Fill rule (``FillMode``). Defaults to non-zero winding.
 257            fillet_radius: Fillet radius when fillets are enabled.
 258            gradient: Optional fill gradient.
 259            line_alpha: Stroke opacity. Unset values use ``runtime_defaults['line_alpha']``.
 260            line_cap: Stroke line cap. Defaults to butt.
 261            line_color: Stroke color. Unset values use ``runtime_defaults['line_color']``.
 262            line_dash_array: Dash pattern.
 263            line_dash_phase: Dash phase offset.
 264            line_join: Stroke line join. Defaults to miter.
 265            line_miter_limit: Miter limit for joins.
 266            line_width: Stroke width. Unset values use ``runtime_defaults['line_width']``.
 267            marker_*: Marker drawing options (same as Shape).
 268            markers_only: If True, draw markers without the path.
 269            smooth: Prefer smooth curve rendering when applicable.
 270
 271        Examples:
 272            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 273            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=sg.pi / 2, line_width=2)
 274            >>> p.angle == sg.pi / 2
 275            True
 276"""
 277
 278        self.pos = start
 279        self.start = start
 280        self.angle = angle  # heading angle
 281        self.operations = []
 282        self.objects = []
 283        super().__init__()
 284        self.subtype = Types.PATH2D
 285        self.cur_shape = Shape([start])
 286        self.append(self.cur_shape)
 287        self.rc = self.r_coord  # alias for r_coord
 288        self.rp = self.r_polar  # alias for rel_polar
 289        self.handles = []
 290        self.stack = deque()
 291
 292        self.closed = False
 293        self._init_from_style_kwargs(
 294            {
 295                "color": color,
 296                "alpha": alpha,
 297                "line_color": line_color,
 298                "fill_color": fill_color,
 299                "line_alpha": line_alpha,
 300                "fill_alpha": fill_alpha,
 301                "line_width": line_width,
 302                "fill": fill,
 303                "stroke": stroke,
 304                "line_dash_array": line_dash_array,
 305                "line_dash_phase": line_dash_phase,
 306                "line_cap": line_cap,
 307                "line_join": line_join,
 308                "line_miter_limit": line_miter_limit,
 309                "smooth": smooth,
 310                "back_style": back_style,
 311                "draw_double": draw_double,
 312                "draw_fillets": draw_fillets,
 313                "double_distance": double_distance,
 314                "double_color": double_color,
 315                "fill_mode": fill_mode,
 316                "fillet_radius": fillet_radius,
 317                "gradient": gradient,
 318                "draw_markers": draw_markers,
 319                "even_odd": even_odd,
 320                "marker_type": marker_type,
 321                "marker_size": marker_size,
 322                "marker_radius": marker_radius,
 323                "marker_alpha": marker_alpha,
 324                "marker_color": marker_color,
 325                "marker_shape": marker_shape,
 326                "markers_only": markers_only,
 327            }
 328        )
 329        self.visible = True
 330
 331    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
 332        """Return True if the path has recorded operations.
 333
 334        A path may still be truthy when the group has no drawable elements yet.
 335
 336        Returns:
 337            True if ``operations`` is non-empty.
 338
 339        Examples:
 340            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 341            >>> bool(sg.Path2D((0, 0)))
 342            False
 343            >>> bool(sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 0)))
 344            True
 345"""
 346        return bool(self.operations)
 347
 348    def __str__(self) -> str:
 349        """Return a string representation of the path.
 350
 351        Returns:
 352            str: The string representation of the path.
 353
 354        Examples:
 355            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 356            >>> str(sg.Path2D()).startswith("Path2D")
 357            True
 358        """
 359        if self.elements is None or len(self.elements) == 0:
 360            res = "Path2D()"
 361        elif len(self.elements) in [1, 2]:
 362            res = f"Path2D({self.elements})"
 363        else:
 364            res = f"Path2D({self.elements[0]}...{self.elements[-1]})"
 365        return res
 366
 367    def __repr__(self) -> str:
 368        """Return a string representation of the path.
 369
 370        Returns:
 371            str: The string representation of the path.
 372
 373        Examples:
 374            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 375            >>> repr(sg.Path2D()) == str(sg.Path2D())
 376            True
 377        """
 378        return self.__str__()
 379
 380    def _create_object(self) -> None:
 381        """Build geometry for the most recently appended operation."""
 382        PO = PathOps
 383        op = self.operations[-1]
 384        op_type = op.subtype
 385        data = op.data
 386        if op_type in _OPEN_SUBPATH_OPS and self.cur_shape.closed:
 387            self.cur_shape = Shape([self.pos])
 388            self.append(self.cur_shape)
 389        if op_type in _MOVE_PATH_OPS:
 390            self.cur_shape = Shape([data])
 391            self.append(self.cur_shape)
 392            self.objects.append(None)
 393        elif op_type in _LINE_PATH_OPS:
 394            self.objects.append(Shape(data))
 395            self.cur_shape.append(data[1])
 396        elif op_type == PO.SEGMENTS:
 397            self.objects.append(Shape(data[1]))
 398            self.cur_shape.extend(data[1])
 399        elif op_type in _SINE_PATH_OPS:
 400            self.objects.append(Shape(data[0]))
 401            self.cur_shape.extend(data[0])
 402        elif op_type in _BEZIER_PATH_OPS:
 403            n_points = runtime_defaults["n_bezier_points"]
 404            curve = Bezier(data, n_points=n_points)
 405            self.objects.append(curve)
 406            self.cur_shape.extend(curve.vertices[1:])
 407            if op_type == PO.CUBIC_TO:
 408                self.handles.extend([(data[0], data[1]), (data[2], data[3])])
 409            else:
 410                self.handles.append((data[0], data[1]))
 411                self.handles.append((data[1], data[2]))
 412        elif op_type == PO.HOBBY_TO:
 413            n_points = runtime_defaults["n_hobby_points"]
 414            start = data[0]
 415            through = list(data[1])
 416            if through and close_points_square(start, through[0]):
 417                through = through[1:]
 418            curve = hobby_shape([start, *through], n_points=n_points)
 419            self.objects.append(Shape(curve.vertices))
 420            self.cur_shape.extend(curve.vertices[1:])
 421        elif op_type in _ARC_PATH_OPS:
 422            self.objects.append(Shape(data[-1]))
 423            self.cur_shape.extend(data[-1][1:])
 424        elif op_type == PO.CLOSE:
 425            self.cur_shape.closed = True
 426            self.objects.append(None)
 427        else:
 428            raise ValueError(f"Invalid operation type: {op_type}")
 429
 430    def copy(self) -> "Path2D":
 431        """Return a deep-enough copy of the path for independent editing.
 432
 433        Returns:
 434            Path2D: Copied path with cloned elements and operations.
 435
 436        Examples:
 437            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 438            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 0))
 439            >>> q = p.copy()
 440            >>> _ = q.line_to((40, 20))
 441            >>> len(p.operations), len(q.operations)
 442            (1, 2)
 443"""
 444
 445        new_path = Path2D(start=self.start)
 446        cur_shape_index = None
 447        for index, element in enumerate(self.elements):
 448            if element is self.cur_shape:
 449                cur_shape_index = index
 450                break
 451
 452        new_path.pos = self.pos
 453        new_path.angle = self.angle
 454        new_path.operations = (
 455            self.operations.copy()
 456        )  # shallow-copy of list is fine if Operations are treated as immutable
 457        new_path.elements = [element.copy() for element in self.elements]
 458        new_path.objects = []
 459        for obj in self.objects:
 460            if obj is not None:
 461                new_path.objects.append(obj.copy())
 462            else:
 463                new_path.objects.append(None)
 464        new_path.even_odd = self.even_odd
 465        new_path.closed = self.closed
 466        if cur_shape_index is not None:
 467            new_path.cur_shape = new_path.elements[cur_shape_index]
 468        else:
 469            new_path.cur_shape = self.cur_shape.copy()
 470        new_path.handles = list(self.handles)
 471        new_path.stack = deque(self.stack)
 472        new_path.copy_style(self)
 473        return new_path
 474
 475    def _add(
 476        self,
 477        pos: PointType,
 478        op: PathOps,
 479        data: object,
 480        pnt2: PointType | None = None,
 481        **kwargs: object,
 482    ) -> None:
 483        """Add an operation and update pen state.
 484
 485        Args:
 486            pos: New pen position after the operation.
 487            op: Path operation kind.
 488            data: Operation payload.
 489            pnt2: Optional point used to update heading. Defaults to None.
 490            **kwargs: ``name`` labels the operation. Other keys are style
 491                overrides applied to the segment.
 492        """
 493        self.operations.append(Operation(op, data))
 494        if op in _HEADING_FROM_DATA_OPS:
 495            self.angle = data[1]
 496        else:
 497            if pnt2 is not None:
 498                self.angle = line_angle(pnt2, pos)
 499            else:
 500                self.angle = line_angle(self.pos, pos)
 501        self._create_object()
 502        style = dict(kwargs)
 503        if "name" in style:
 504            setattr(self, style["name"], self.operations[-1])
 505            del style["name"]
 506        targets = []
 507        segment = self.objects[-1]
 508        if segment is not None:
 509            targets.append(segment)
 510        if self.cur_shape is not None and self.cur_shape is not segment:
 511            targets.append(self.cur_shape)
 512        for target in targets:
 513            for key, value in style.items():
 514                setattr(target, key, value)
 515        list(pos)[:2]
 516        self.pos = pos
 517
 518    @property
 519    def all_vertices(self) -> list:
 520        """Return all vertices of the path after applying transforms.
 521
 522        Returns:
 523            list: Flattened vertex list.
 524
 525        Examples:
 526            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 527            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 0)).line_to((40, 20))
 528            >>> [[round(c, 6) for c in q[:2]] for q in p.all_vertices]
 529            [[0.0, 0.0], [40.0, 0.0], [40.0, 0.0], [40.0, 20.0]]
 530"""
 531        all_vertices = []
 532        for obj in self.objects:
 533            if obj is not None:
 534                all_vertices.extend(obj.vertices)
 535
 536        return all_vertices
 537
 538    @property
 539    def all_elements(self) -> list:
 540        """Return the transformed geometric objects that make up the path.
 541
 542        Returns:
 543            list: Drawable elements in the path group.
 544
 545        Examples:
 546            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 547            >>> path = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 0))
 548            >>> [[round(float(c), 6) or 0.0 for c in q[:2]] for q in path.all_elements[0].vertices]
 549            [[0.0, 0.0], [40.0, 0.0]]
 550        """
 551        return [obj for obj in self.objects if obj is not None]
 552
 553    @property
 554    def sections(self) -> list:
 555        """Geometric sections of the path (alias of ``all_elements``).
 556
 557        Each drawing operation that produces geometry is one section
 558        (``line_to``, ``cubic_to``, ``arc``, …). ``move_to`` and ``close``
 559        do not create sections.
 560
 561        Returns:
 562            list: The same objects as ``all_elements``.
 563
 564        Examples:
 565            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 566            >>> path = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 0)).line_to((40, 20))
 567            >>> len(path.sections)
 568            2
 569            >>> path.sections[0] is path.all_elements[0]
 570            True
 571        """
 572        return self.all_elements
 573
 574    def uniform_points(
 575        self,
 576        distance: float,
 577        align_section_ends: bool = True,
 578        align_path_end: bool = True,
 579        rel_tol: float | None = None,
 580        abs_tol: float | None = None,
 581    ) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
 582        """Return points spaced by ``distance`` along the path.
 583
 584        Sampling restarts on each section. A section end is included when
 585        the leftover stub is within tolerance of ``distance`` (or of 0),
 586        or when the matching align flag is True. On the last section,
 587        ``align_path_end`` is used instead of ``align_section_ends``.
 588        Connected section starts are not repeated; a new subpath start is.
 589
 590        Args:
 591            distance: Arc-length spacing. Must be positive.
 592            align_section_ends: If True, always include each non-final
 593                section end. Defaults to True.
 594            align_path_end: If True, always include the path end.
 595                Defaults to True.
 596            rel_tol: Relative leftover tolerance. ``None`` uses
 597                ``runtime_defaults["rel_tol"]``.
 598            abs_tol: Absolute leftover tolerance. ``None`` uses
 599                ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
 600
 601        Returns:
 602            list[tuple[float, float]]: Sample points in path order.
 603
 604        Raises:
 605            ValueError: If ``distance`` is not positive.
 606
 607        Examples:
 608            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 609            >>> path = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 0))
 610            >>> path.uniform_points(20)
 611            [(0.0, 0.0), (20.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0)]
 612            >>> path.uniform_points(20, align_path_end=False)
 613            [(0.0, 0.0), (20.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0)]
 614            >>> corner = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 0)).line_to((40, 20))
 615            >>> corner.uniform_points(20)
 616            [(0.0, 0.0), (20.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 20.0)]
 617            >>> corner.uniform_points(20, align_section_ends=False)
 618            [(0.0, 0.0), (20.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 20.0)]
 619            >>> path.uniform_points(20, True, True, 0, 0.001)[-1]
 620            (40.0, 0.0)
 621            >>> path.uniform_points(0)
 622            Traceback (most recent call last):
 623                ...
 624            ValueError: distance must be positive
 625        """
 626        if distance <= 0:
 627            raise ValueError("distance must be positive")
 628        rel_tol, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
 629        abs_tol2 = abs_tol * abs_tol
 630
 631        def lengths_close(first: float, second: float) -> bool:
 632            return bool(
 633                np.isclose(first, second, rtol=rel_tol, atol=abs_tol)
 634            )
 635
 636        def append_unique(
 637            points: list[tuple[float, float]], point: PointType
 638        ) -> None:
 639            xy = _xy_point(point)
 640            if points and close_points_square(points[-1], xy, abs_tol2):
 641                return
 642            points.append(xy)
 643
 644        points: list[tuple[float, float]] = []
 645        previous_end: tuple[float, float] | None = None
 646        sections = self.sections
 647        last_index = len(sections) - 1
 648        for index, section in enumerate(sections):
 649            vertices = list(section.vertices)
 650            if not vertices:
 651                continue
 652            start = _xy_point(vertices[0])
 653            end = _xy_point(vertices[-1])
 654            connected = previous_end is not None and close_points_square(
 655                previous_end, start, abs_tol2
 656            )
 657            if not connected:
 658                append_unique(points, start)
 659            if len(vertices) < 2:
 660                previous_end = end
 661                continue
 662            section_length = polyline_length(
 663                vertices, closed=False, abs_tol=abs_tol
 664            )
 665            last_s = 0.0
 666            while True:
 667                next_s = last_s + distance
 668                if next_s > section_length or lengths_close(
 669                    next_s, section_length
 670                ):
 671                    break
 672                append_unique(
 673                    points, _polyline_point_at_length(vertices, next_s)
 674                )
 675                last_s = next_s
 676            leftover = section_length - last_s
 677            align_end = (
 678                align_path_end if index == last_index else align_section_ends
 679            )
 680            if lengths_close(leftover, 0.0):
 681                pass
 682            elif lengths_close(leftover, distance) or align_end:
 683                append_unique(points, end)
 684            previous_end = end
 685        return points
 686
 687    @property
 688    def b_box(self) -> BoundingBox:
 689        """Return the axis-aligned bounding box of the path.
 690
 691        Returns:
 692            Bounding box of all path vertices.
 693
 694        Examples:
 695            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 696            >>> box = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 20)).b_box
 697            >>> box.width, box.height
 698            (40.0, 20.0)
 699"""
 700
 701        return bounding_box(self.all_vertices)
 702
 703    def push(self) -> None:
 704        """Push the current pen position and heading onto the stack.
 705
 706        Examples:
 707            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 708            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=0)
 709            >>> p.push()
 710            >>> _ = p.forward(40)
 711            >>> p.pop()
 712            >>> p.pos
 713            (0, 0)
 714"""
 715        self.stack.append((self.pos, self.angle))
 716
 717    def pop(self) -> None:
 718        """Restore the pen position and heading from the stack.
 719
 720        Starts a new subpath at the restored position so later drawing is
 721        not connected to the segment that was drawn after ``push``. Does
 722        nothing if the stack is empty.
 723
 724        Examples:
 725            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 726            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=0)
 727            >>> p.push()
 728            >>> _ = p.forward(20).turn(sg.pi / 2)
 729            >>> p.pop()
 730            >>> p.angle
 731            0
 732            >>> p.pos
 733            (0, 0)
 734"""
 735        if not self.stack:
 736            return
 737        pos, angle = self.stack.pop()
 738        self.operations.append(Operation(PathOps.MOVE_TO, pos))
 739        self._create_object()
 740        self.pos = pos
 741        self.angle = angle
 742
 743    def r_coord(self, dx: float, dy: float) -> PointType:
 744        """Map local offsets into world coordinates relative to the pen.
 745
 746        The local y-axis is aligned with the current heading.
 747
 748        Args:
 749            dx: Offset along the local x-axis.
 750            dy: Offset along the local y-axis (heading direction).
 751
 752        Returns:
 753            PointType: Absolute point.
 754
 755        Examples:
 756            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 757            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=sg.pi / 2)
 758            >>> x, y = p.r_coord(0, 40)
 759            >>> round(x, 6), round(y, 6)
 760            (0.0, 40.0)
 761"""
 762        x, y = self.pos[:2]
 763        theta = self.angle - pi / 2
 764        x1 = dx * cos(theta) - dy * sin(theta) + x
 765        y1 = dx * sin(theta) + dy * cos(theta) + y
 766
 767        return x1, y1
 768
 769    def r_polar(self, r: float, angle: float) -> PointType:
 770        """Return an absolute point from polar offsets relative to the pen.
 771
 772        Angle ``0`` is aligned with the current heading.
 773
 774        Args:
 775            r: Radius.
 776            angle: Angle in radians relative to the heading.
 777
 778        Returns:
 779            PointType: Absolute point.
 780
 781        Examples:
 782            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 783            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=sg.pi / 2)
 784            >>> x, y = p.r_polar(40, 0)
 785            >>> round(x, 6), round(y, 6)
 786            (40.0, 0.0)
 787"""
 788        x, y = polar_to_cartesian(r, angle + self.angle - pi / 2)[:2]
 789        x1, y1 = self.pos[:2]
 790
 791        return x1 + x, y1 + y
 792
 793    def line_to(self, point: PointType, **kwargs: object) -> Self:
 794        """Draw a straight segment from the current position to ``point``.
 795
 796        Args:
 797            point: Absolute end point.
 798            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
 799
 800        Returns:
 801            Self: This path (for chaining).
 802
 803        Examples:
 804            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 805            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 0))
 806            >>> p.pos
 807            (40, 0)
 808"""
 809        self._add(point, PathOps.LINE_TO, (self.pos, point), **kwargs)
 810
 811        return self
 812
 813    def forward(self, length: float, **kwargs: object) -> Self:
 814        """Advance the pen ``length`` units along the current heading.
 815
 816        Args:
 817            length: Distance to travel.
 818            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
 819
 820        Returns:
 821            Self: This path (for chaining).
 822
 823        Examples:
 824            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 825            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=0).forward(40)
 826            >>> p.pos
 827            (40.0, 0.0)
 828"""
 829
 830        x, y = line_by_point_angle_length(self.pos, self.angle, length)[1][:2]
 831        self._add((x, y), PathOps.FORWARD, (self.pos, (x, y)), **kwargs)
 832
 833        return self
 834
 835    def orient(self, angle: float) -> Self:
 836        """Set the absolute heading angle.
 837
 838        Args:
 839            angle: New heading in radians.
 840
 841        Returns:
 842            Self: This path.
 843
 844        Examples:
 845            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 846            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).orient(sg.pi)
 847            >>> p.angle == sg.pi
 848            True
 849"""
 850        self.angle = angle
 851
 852        return self
 853
 854    def turn(self, angle: float, distance: float = 0) -> Self:
 855        """Turn by ``angle`` radians, optionally moving ``distance`` forward.
 856
 857        Args:
 858            angle: Heading increment in radians.
 859            distance: Optional forward distance after the turn. Defaults to 0.
 860
 861        Returns:
 862            Self: This path.
 863
 864        Examples:
 865            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 866            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=0).turn(sg.pi / 2, distance=40)
 867            >>> round(p.pos[0], 6), round(p.pos[1], 6)
 868            (0.0, 40.0)
 869"""
 870
 871        self.angle += angle
 872        if distance != 0:
 873            self.forward(distance)
 874
 875        return self

 877    def move(
 878        self,
 879        pos: PointType,
 880        anchor: Anchor = Anchor.CENTER,
 881        **kwargs: object,
 882    ) -> Self:
 883        """Translate the whole path so a bbox anchor sits at ``pos``.
 884
 885        Args:
 886            pos: Target location for the chosen anchor.
 887            anchor: Bounding-box anchor (default ``Anchor.CENTER``).
 888            **kwargs: Extra attributes set on the path before transforming.
 889
 890        Returns:
 891            Self or Group: Transformed path (or group when repetitions apply).
 892
 893        Examples:
 894            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 895            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 0))
 896            >>> _ = p.move((50, 50))
 897            >>> abs(p.b_box.center[0] - 50) < 1e-6
 898            True
 899"""
 900        x, y = pos[:2]
 901        anchor = get_enum_value(Anchor, anchor)
 902        x1, y1 = getattr(self.b_box, anchor)
 903        transform = translation_matrix(x - x1, y - y1)
 904        for k, v in kwargs.items():
 905            setattr(self, k, v)
 906        res = self._update(transform, reps=0)
 907
 908        return res
 909
 910    def move_to(self, point: PointType, **kwargs: object) -> Self:
 911        """Lift the pen and start a new subpath at ``point``.
 912
 913        Args:
 914            point: Absolute destination.
 915            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
 916
 917        Returns:
 918            Self: This path.
 919
 920        Examples:
 921            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 922            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((20, 0)).move_to((0, 20))
 923            >>> p.pos
 924            (0, 20)
 925"""
 926        self._add(point, PathOps.MOVE_TO, point)
 927
 928        return self

 930    def r_line(self, dx: float, dy: float, **kwargs: object) -> Self:
 931        """Draw a line using relative offsets from the current position.
 932
 933        Args:
 934            dx: X offset.
 935            dy: Y offset.
 936            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
 937
 938        Returns:
 939            Self: This path.
 940
 941        Examples:
 942            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 943            >>> p = sg.Path2D((40, 40)).r_line(60, 80)
 944            >>> p.pos
 945            (100, 120)
 946"""
 947        point = self.pos[0] + dx, self.pos[1] + dy
 948        self._add(point, PathOps.R_LINE, (self.pos, point), **kwargs)
 949
 950        return self

 952    def r_move(self, dx: float = 0, dy: float = 0, **kwargs: object) -> Self:
 953        """Move the pen by relative offsets without drawing.
 954
 955        Args:
 956            dx: X offset. Defaults to 0.
 957            dy: Y offset. Defaults to 0.
 958            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
 959
 960        Returns:
 961            Self: This path.
 962
 963        Examples:
 964            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 965            >>> p = sg.Path2D((40, 40)).r_move(80, 60)
 966            >>> p.pos
 967            (120, 100)
 968"""
 969        x, y = self.pos[:2]
 970        point = (x + dx, y + dy)
 971        self._add(point, PathOps.R_MOVE, point, **kwargs)
 972        return self

 974    def h_line_to(self, x: float, **kwargs: object) -> Self:
 975        """Draw a horizontal line to absolute x, keeping the current y.
 976
 977        Args:
 978            x: Absolute x coordinate of the end point.
 979            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
 980
 981        Returns:
 982            Self: This path.
 983
 984        Examples:
 985            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 986            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 80)).h_line_to(80)
 987            >>> p.pos
 988            (80, 80)
 989"""
 990        y = self.pos[1]
 991        self._add((x, y), PathOps.H_LINE_TO, (self.pos, (x, y)), **kwargs)
 992        return self

 994    def r_h_line(self, length: float, **kwargs: object) -> Self:
 995        """Draw a horizontal line of the given length.

 998            length: Signed horizontal distance.

1001        Returns:

1004        Examples:
1005            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg

1007            >>> p.pos
1008            (40, 0)

1010        x, y = self.pos[0] + length, self.pos[1]

1014    def v_line_to(self, y: float, **kwargs: object) -> Self:

1034    def r_v_line(self, length: float, **kwargs: object) -> Self:
1035        """Draw a vertical line of the given length.

1038            length: Signed vertical distance.

1040

1054    def segments(
1055        self, points: Sequence[PointType], **kwargs: object
1056    ) -> Self:
1057        """Append polyline segments through absolute ``points``.
1058
1059        Args:
1060            points: Sequence of absolute points.
1061            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1062
1063        Returns:
1064            Self: This path.
1065
1066        Examples:
1067            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1068            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).segments([(20, 0), (20, 20)])
1069            >>> p.pos
1070            (20, 20)
1071"""
1072
1073        self._add(
1074            points[-1],
1075            PathOps.SEGMENTS,
1076            (self.pos, points),
1077            pnt2=points[-2],
1078            **kwargs,
1079        )

1082    def cubic_to(
1083        self,
1084        control1: PointType,
1085        control2: PointType,
1086        end: PointType,
1087        **kwargs: object,
1088    ) -> Self:
1089        """Append a cubic Bézier from the current position to ``end``.
1090
1091        Args:
1092            control1: First control point.
1093            control2: Second control point.
1094            end: Curve end point.
1095            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1096
1097        Returns:
1098            Self: This path.
1099
1100        Examples:
1101            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1102            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).cubic_to((40, 80), (60, 80), (80, 0))
1103            >>> p.pos
1104            (80, 0)
1105"""
1106        self._add(
1107            end,
1108            PathOps.CUBIC_TO,
1109            (self.pos, control1, control2, end),
1110            pnt2=control2,
1111            **kwargs,
1112        )
1113        return self
1114
1115    def r_cubic_to(
1116        self,
1117        r_control1: PointType,
1118        r_control2: PointType,
1119        r_end: PointType,
1120        **kwargs: object,
1121    ) -> Self:
1122        """Append a cubic Bézier with relative control points and end (SVG ``c``).
1123
1124        Args:
1125            r_control1: First control offset ``(dx, dy)`` from the pen.
1126            r_control2: Second control offset ``(dx, dy)`` from the pen.
1127            r_end: End offset ``(dx, dy)`` from the pen.
1128            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1129
1130        Returns:
1131            Self: This path.
1132
1133        Examples:
1134            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1135            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).r_cubic_to((40, 80), (60, 80), (80, 0))
1136            >>> p.pos
1137            (80, 0)
1138"""
1139        cur_x, cur_y = self.pos
1140        control1 = (cur_x + r_control1[0], cur_y + r_control1[1])
1141        control2 = (cur_x + r_control2[0], cur_y + r_control2[1])
1142        end = (cur_x + r_end[0], cur_y + r_end[1])
1143        return self.cubic_to(control1, control2, end, **kwargs)
1144
1145    def r_segments(
1146        self, r_points: Sequence[PointType], **kwargs: object
1147    ) -> Self:
1148        """Append polyline segments using successive ``(dx, dy)`` offsets.
1149
1150        Args:
1151            r_points: Sequence of relative offsets.
1152            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1153
1154        Returns:
1155            Self: This path.
1156
1157        Examples:
1158            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1159            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).r_segments([(20, 0), (0, 20)])
1160            >>> p.pos
1161            (20, 20)
1162"""
1163        # Convert relative offsets to absolute points
1164        points = []
1165        current_x, current_y = self.pos
1166        for dx, dy in r_points:
1167            current_x += dx
1168            current_y += dy
1169            points.append((current_x, current_y))
1170
1171        self._add(
1172            points[-1],
1173            PathOps.SEGMENTS,
1174            (self.pos, points),
1175            pnt2=points[-2],
1176            **kwargs,
1177        )
1178        return self
1179
1180    def hobby_to(
1181        self, points: Sequence[PointType], **kwargs: object
1182    ) -> Self:
1183        """Append a Hobby smooth curve through ``points``.
1184
1185        If the first point is the current pen position, it is not repeated.
1186
1187        Args:
1188            points: Curve points. The first point may be the current position.
1189            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1190
1191        Returns:
1192            Self: This path.
1193
1194        Examples:
1195            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1196            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).hobby_to([(40, 20), (20, 0)])
1197            >>> p.pos
1198            (20, 0)
1199            >>> q = sg.Path2D().hobby_to([(0, 0), (40, 20), (20, 0)])
1200            >>> q.pos
1201            (20, 0)
1202"""
1203        self._add(points[-1], PathOps.HOBBY_TO, (self.pos, points), **kwargs)
1204        return self

1206    def quad_to(
1207        self,
1208        control: PointType,
1209        end: PointType,
1210        *args: object,
1211        **kwargs: object,
1212    ) -> Self:
1213        """Append a quadratic Bézier to ``end`` with control point ``control``.
1214
1215        Additional ``*args`` entries can continue the curve as blended quads.
1216
1217        Args:
1218            control: Control point.
1219            end: Curve end point.
1220            *args: Either ``(length, end)`` or ``(control, end)`` pairs.
1221            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1222
1223        Returns:
1224            Self: This path.
1225
1226        Raises:
1227            ValueError: If an ``*args`` entry does not have exactly two items.
1228
1229        Examples:
1230            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1231            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).quad_to((20, 20), (40, 0))
1232            >>> p.pos
1233            (40, 0)
1234"""
1235        self._add(
1236            end,
1237            PathOps.QUAD_TO,
1238            (self.pos[:2], control, end[:2]),
1239            pnt2=control,
1240            **kwargs,
1241        )
1242        pos = end
1243        for arg in args:
1244            if len(arg) != 2:
1245                raise ValueError("Invalid number of arguments for curve.")
1246            if isinstance(arg[0], (int, float)):
1247                # (length, end)
1248                length = arg[0]
1249                control = extended_line(length, control, pos)
1250                end = arg[1]
1251                self._add(
1252                    end, PathOps.QUAD_TO, (pos, control, end), pnt2=control
1253                )
1254                pos = end
1255            elif isinstance(arg[0], (list, tuple)):
1256                # (control, end)
1257                control = arg[0]
1258                end = arg[1]
1259                self._add(
1260                    end, PathOps.QUAD_TO, (pos, control, end), pnt2=control
1261                )
1262                pos = end
1263        return self
1264
1265    def r_quad_to(
1266        self,
1267        r_control: PointType,
1268        r_end: PointType,
1269        **kwargs: object,
1270    ) -> Self:
1271        """Append a quadratic Bézier with relative control and end (SVG ``q``).
1272
1273        Args:
1274            r_control: Control offset ``(dx, dy)`` from the pen.
1275            r_end: End offset ``(dx, dy)`` from the pen.
1276            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1277
1278        Returns:
1279            Self: This path.
1280
1281        Examples:
1282            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1283            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).r_quad_to((20, 20), (40, 0))
1284            >>> p.pos
1285            (40, 0)
1286"""
1287        cur_x, cur_y = self.pos
1288        control = (cur_x + r_control[0], cur_y + r_control[1])
1289        end = (cur_x + r_end[0], cur_y + r_end[1])
1290        return self.quad_to(control, end, **kwargs)
1291
1292    def mirror_cubic_to(
1293        self, control2: PointType, end: PointType, **kwargs: object
1294    ) -> Self:
1295        """Append a smooth cubic Bézier (SVG ``S``).
1296
1297        Mirrors the previous second control point across the current position
1298        to obtain the first control point.
1299
1300        Args:
1301            control2: Second control point.
1302            end: Curve end point.
1303            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1304
1305        Returns:
1306            Self: This path.
1307
1308        Examples:
1309            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1310            >>> p = (
1311            ... sg.Path2D((0, 0))
1312            ... .cubic_to((40, 80), (60, 80), (80, 0))
1313            ... .mirror_cubic_to((20, -80), (80, 0))
1314            ... )
1315            >>> p.pos
1316            (80, 0)
1317"""
1318        # Get previous control point from last operation if it was a cubic
1319        prev_c2 = self.pos
1320        last_op = self.operations[-1] if self.operations else None
1321        if last_op and last_op.subtype in _CUBIC_PATH_OPS:
1322            # data: (start, c1, c2, end)
1323            prev_c2 = last_op.data[2]
1324
1325        # Mirror prev_c2 across current position
1326        cur_x, cur_y = self.pos
1327        c1_x = 2 * cur_x - prev_c2[0]
1328        c1_y = 2 * cur_y - prev_c2[1]
1329        control1 = (c1_x, c1_y)
1330
1331        self._add(
1332            end,
1333            PathOps.CUBIC_TO,
1334            (self.pos, control1, control2, end),
1335            pnt2=control2,
1336            **kwargs,
1337        )
1338        return self
1339
1340    def r_mirror_cubic_to(
1341        self, r_control2: PointType, r_end: PointType, **kwargs: object
1342    ) -> Self:
1343        """Append a relative smooth cubic Bézier (SVG ``s``).
1344
1345        Args:
1346            r_control2: Relative second control point ``(dx, dy)``.
1347            r_end: Relative end point ``(dx, dy)``.
1348            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1349
1350        Returns:
1351            Self: This path.
1352
1353        Examples:
1354            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1355            >>> p = (
1356            ... sg.Path2D((0, 0))
1357            ... .cubic_to((40, 80), (60, 80), (80, 0))
1358            ... .r_mirror_cubic_to((40, -80), (80, 0))
1359            ... )
1360            >>> p.pos
1361            (160, 0)
1362"""
1363        cur_x, cur_y = self.pos
1364        control2 = (cur_x + r_control2[0], cur_y + r_control2[1])
1365        end = (cur_x + r_end[0], cur_y + r_end[1])
1366        return self.mirror_cubic_to(control2, end, **kwargs)
1367
1368    def mirror_quad_to(self, end: PointType, **kwargs: object) -> Self:
1369        """Append a smooth quadratic Bézier (SVG ``T``).
1370
1371        Args:
1372            end: Curve end point.
1373            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1374
1375        Returns:
1376            Self: This path.
1377
1378        Examples:
1379            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1380            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).quad_to((20, 20), (40, 0)).mirror_quad_to((20, 0))
1381            >>> p.pos
1382            (20, 0)
1383"""
1384        # Get previous control point from last operation if it was a quad
1385        prev_c1 = self.pos
1386        last_op = self.operations[-1] if self.operations else None
1387        if last_op and last_op.subtype in _QUAD_PATH_OPS:
1388            # data: (start, c1, end)
1389            prev_c1 = last_op.data[1]
1390
1391        # Mirror prev_c1 across current position
1392        cur_x, cur_y = self.pos
1393        c1_x = 2 * cur_x - prev_c1[0]
1394        c1_y = 2 * cur_y - prev_c1[1]
1395        control = (c1_x, c1_y)
1396
1397        self._add(
1398            end,
1399            PathOps.QUAD_TO,
1400            (self.pos[:2], control, end[:2]),
1401            pnt2=control,
1402            **kwargs,
1403        )
1404        return self
1405
1406    def r_mirror_quad_to(self, r_end: PointType, **kwargs: object) -> Self:
1407        """Append a relative smooth quadratic Bézier (SVG ``t``).
1408
1409        Args:
1410            r_end: Relative end point ``(dx, dy)``.
1411            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1412
1413        Returns:
1414            Self: This path.
1415
1416        Examples:
1417            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1418            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).quad_to((20, 20), (40, 0)).r_mirror_quad_to((40, 0))
1419            >>> p.pos
1420            (80, 0)
1421"""
1422        cur_x, cur_y = self.pos
1423        end = (cur_x + r_end[0], cur_y + r_end[1])
1424        return self.mirror_quad_to(end, **kwargs)
1425
1426    def blend_cubic(
1427        self,
1428        control1_length: float,
1429        control2: PointType,
1430        end: PointType,
1431        **kwargs: object,
1432    ) -> Self:
1433        """Append a cubic Bézier whose first control lies along the heading.
1434
1435        Args:
1436            control1_length: Distance from the pen to the first control point.
1437            control2: Second control point.
1438            end: Curve end point.
1439            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1440
1441        Returns:
1442            Self: This path.
1443
1444        Examples:
1445            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1446            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=0).blend_cubic(40, (80, 80), (60, 0))
1447            >>> p.pos
1448            (60, 0)
1449"""
1450        c1 = line_by_point_angle_length(self.pos, self.angle, control1_length)[
1451            1
1452        ]
1453        self._add(
1454            end,
1455            PathOps.CUBIC_TO,
1456            (self.pos, c1, control2, end),
1457            pnt2=control2,
1458            **kwargs,
1459        )
1460        return self
1461
1462    def blend_quad(
1463        self, control_length: float, end: PointType, **kwargs: object
1464    ) -> Self:
1465        """Append a quadratic Bézier whose control lies along the heading.
1466
1467        Args:
1468            control_length: Distance from the pen to the control point.
1469            end: Curve end point.
1470            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1471
1472        Returns:
1473            Self: This path.
1474
1475        Examples:
1476            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1477            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=0).blend_quad(40, (40, 0))
1478            >>> p.pos
1479            (40, 0)
1480"""
1481        pos = list(self.pos[:2])
1482        c1 = line_by_point_angle_length(pos, self.angle, control_length)[1]
1483        self._add(end, PathOps.QUAD_TO, (pos, c1, end), pnt2=c1, **kwargs)
1484        return self
1485
1486    @alias_argument({"radius_x": "rx", "radius_y": "ry"})
1487    def arc(
1488        self,
1489        radius_x: float,
1490        radius_y: float | None = None,
1491        start_angle: float = 0,
1492        span_angle: float | None = None,
1493        rot_angle: float = 0,
1494        n_points: int | None = None,
1495        *,
1496        end_angle: float | None = None,
1497        clockwise: bool = False,
1498        **kwargs: object,
1499    ) -> Self:
1500        """Append an elliptic arc starting at the current pen position.
1501
1502        Pass either ``span_angle`` or ``end_angle``, not both. Use
1503        ``clockwise=True`` or a negative ``span_angle`` for a clockwise
1504        arc.
1505
1506        Args:
1507            radius_x: Ellipse half-width.
1508            radius_y: Ellipse half-height; defaults to ``radius_x``.
1509            start_angle: Arc start angle in radians. Defaults to 0.
1510            span_angle: Sweep in radians. A negative value draws clockwise.
1511                Mutually exclusive with ``end_angle``. At least one of
1512                ``span_angle`` or ``end_angle`` is required.
1513            rot_angle: Ellipse rotation in radians. Defaults to 0.
1514            n_points: Sample count; defaults to ``runtime_defaults['n_arc_points']``.
1515            end_angle: Ending angle in radians. Mutually exclusive with
1516                ``span_angle``.
1517            clockwise: If True, the arc is drawn clockwise. Defaults to False.
1518            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1519
1520        Returns:
1521            Self: This path.
1522
1523        Examples:
1524            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1525            >>> p = sg.Path2D((40, 0), angle=0).arc(40, 40, 0, sg.pi / 2)
1526            >>> round(float(p.pos[0]), 5), round(float(p.pos[1]), 5)
1527            (0.0, 40.0)
1528            >>> p = sg.Path2D((40, 0), angle=0).arc(40, 40, 0, -sg.pi / 2)
1529            >>> round(float(p.pos[0]), 5) or 0.0, round(float(p.pos[1]), 5)
1530            (0.0, -40.0)
1531"""
1532        if radius_y is None:
1533            radius_y = radius_x
1534        rx = radius_x
1535        ry = radius_y
1536        start_angle = positive_angle(start_angle)
1537        signed_span = resolve_arc_sweep(
1538            start_angle, span_angle, end_angle, clockwise
1539        )
1540        clockwise = signed_span < 0
1541        if n_points is None:
1542            n_points = runtime_defaults["n_arc_points"]
1543        points = _elliptic_arc_points_from_signed(
1544            (0, 0), rx, ry, start_angle, signed_span, n_points
1545        )
1546        start = points[0]
1547        end = points[-1]
1548        # Translate the start to the current position and rotate by the rotation angle.
1549        dx = self.pos[0] - start[0]
1550        dy = self.pos[1] - start[1]
1551        rotocenter = start
1552        if rot_angle != 0:
1553            points = (
1554                homogenize(points)
1555                @ rotation_matrix(rot_angle, rotocenter)
1556                @ translation_matrix(dx, dy)
1557            )
1558        else:
1559            points = homogenize(points) @ translation_matrix(dx, dy)
1560        tangent_angle = ellipse_tangent(rx, ry, *end) + rot_angle
1561        if clockwise:
1562            tangent_angle += pi
1563        pos = points[-1]
1564        self._add(
1565            pos,
1566            PathOps.ARC,
1567            (
1568                pos,
1569                tangent_angle,
1570                rx,
1571                ry,
1572                start_angle,
1573                signed_span,
1574                rot_angle,
1575                points,
1576            ),
1577            **kwargs,
1578        )
1579        return self
1580
1581    def arc_to(
1582        self,
1583        rx: float,
1584        ry: float,
1585        angle: float,
1586        large_arc_flag: bool,
1587        sweep_flag: bool,
1588        end: PointType,
1589        **kwargs: object,
1590    ) -> Self:
1591        """Append an SVG-style elliptical arc to ``end`` (SVG ``A``).
1592
1593        Args:
1594            rx: Ellipse x-radius.
1595            ry: Ellipse y-radius.
1596            angle: Ellipse rotation in degrees.
1597            large_arc_flag: Use the large arc if True.
1598            sweep_flag: SVG sweep flag.
1599            end: Absolute end point.
1600            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1601
1602        Returns:
1603            Self: This path.
1604
1605        Examples:
1606            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1607            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).arc_to(40, 40, 0, False, True, (40, 40))
1608            >>> [round(float(c), 5) for c in p.pos[:2]]
1609            [40.0, 40.0]
1610            >>> [round(float(c), 5) for c in p.vertices[0][:2]], [round(float(c), 5) for c in p.vertices[-1][:2]]
1611            ([0.0, 0.0], [40.0, 40.0])
1612"""
1613        params = _get_svg_arc_params(
1614            self.pos, rx, ry, angle, large_arc_flag, sweep_flag, end
1615        )
1616
1617        if params is not None and params[0] is PathOps.LINE_TO:
1618            self.line_to(params[1], **kwargs)
1619        elif params is not None and params[0] is PathOps.ARC:
1620            (
1621                _op,
1622                radius_x,
1623                radius_y,
1624                start_angle,
1625                span_angle,
1626                rot_angle,
1627            ) = params
1628            signed_span = span_angle
1629            self.arc(
1630                radius_x,
1631                radius_y,
1632                start_angle,
1633                abs(signed_span),
1634                rot_angle=rot_angle,
1635                clockwise=signed_span < 0,
1636                **kwargs,
1637            )
1638        return self
1639
1640    def r_arc_to(
1641        self,
1642        rx: float,
1643        ry: float,
1644        angle: float,
1645        large_arc_flag: bool,
1646        sweep_flag: bool,
1647        r_end: PointType,
1648        **kwargs: object,
1649    ) -> Self:
1650        """Append an SVG-style elliptical arc with a relative end (SVG ``a``).
1651
1652        Radii, rotation, and flags match SVG ``a``; only ``r_end`` is an offset
1653        from the current pen.
1654
1655        Args:
1656            rx: Ellipse x-radius.
1657            ry: Ellipse y-radius.
1658            angle: Ellipse rotation in degrees.
1659            large_arc_flag: Use the large arc if True.
1660            sweep_flag: SVG sweep flag.
1661            r_end: End offset ``(dx, dy)`` from the pen.
1662            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1663
1664        Returns:
1665            Self: This path.
1666
1667        Examples:
1668            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1669            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).r_arc_to(40, 40, 0, False, True, (40, 40))
1670            >>> round(float(p.pos[0]), 5), round(float(p.pos[1]), 5)
1671            (40.0, 40.0)
1672"""
1673        cur_x, cur_y = self.pos[:2]
1674        end = (cur_x + r_end[0], cur_y + r_end[1])
1675        return self.arc_to(
1676            rx, ry, angle, large_arc_flag, sweep_flag, end, **kwargs
1677        )
1678
1679    @alias_argument({"radius_x": "rx", "radius_y": "ry"})
1680    def blend_arc(
1681        self,
1682        radius_x: float,
1683        radius_y: float | None = None,
1684        start_angle: float = 0,
1685        span_angle: float | None = None,
1686        sharp: bool = False,
1687        n_points: int | None = None,
1688        *,
1689        end_angle: float | None = None,
1690        clockwise: bool = False,
1691        **kwargs: object,
1692    ) -> Self:
1693        """Append an elliptic arc blended to the current heading.
1694
1695        Pass either ``span_angle`` or ``end_angle``, not both. Use
1696        ``clockwise=True`` or a negative ``span_angle`` for a clockwise
1697        arc.
1698
1699        Args:
1700            radius_x: Ellipse half-width.
1701            radius_y: Ellipse half-height; defaults to ``radius_x``.
1702            start_angle: Arc start angle in radians. Defaults to 0.
1703            span_angle: Sweep in radians. A negative value draws clockwise.
1704                Mutually exclusive with ``end_angle``. At least one of
1705                ``span_angle`` or ``end_angle`` is required.
1706            sharp: Flip the blend orientation if True. Defaults to False.
1707            n_points: Sample count; defaults to ``runtime_defaults['n_arc_points']``.
1708            end_angle: Ending angle in radians. Mutually exclusive with
1709                ``span_angle``.
1710            clockwise: If True, the arc is drawn clockwise. Defaults to False.
1711            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1712
1713        Returns:
1714            Self: This path.
1715
1716        Examples:
1717            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1718            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=0).blend_arc(40, 40, 0, sg.pi / 2)
1719            >>> [round(float(c), 5) for c in p.pos[:2]]
1720            [40.0, 40.0]
1721            >>> [round(float(c), 5) for c in p.vertices[0][:2]], [round(float(c), 5) for c in p.vertices[-1][:2]]
1722            ([0.0, 0.0], [40.0, 40.0])
1723"""
1724        if radius_y is None:
1725            radius_y = radius_x
1726        rx = radius_x
1727        ry = radius_y
1728        start_angle = positive_angle(start_angle)
1729        signed_span = resolve_arc_sweep(
1730            start_angle, span_angle, end_angle, clockwise
1731        )
1732        clockwise = signed_span < 0
1733        if n_points is None:
1734            n_points = runtime_defaults["n_arc_points"]
1735        points = _elliptic_arc_points_from_signed(
1736            (0, 0), rx, ry, start_angle, signed_span, n_points
1737        )
1738        start = points[0]
1739        end = points[-1]
1740        # Translate the start to the current position and rotate by the computed rotation angle.
1741        dx = self.pos[0] - start[0]
1742        dy = self.pos[1] - start[1]
1743        rotocenter = start
1744        tangent = ellipse_tangent(rx, ry, *start)
1745        rot_angle = self.angle - tangent
1746        if clockwise:
1747            rot_angle += pi
1748        if sharp:
1749            rot_angle += pi
1750        points = (
1751            homogenize(points)
1752            @ rotation_matrix(rot_angle, rotocenter)
1753            @ translation_matrix(dx, dy)
1754        )
1755        tangent_angle = ellipse_tangent(rx, ry, *end) + rot_angle
1756        if clockwise:
1757            tangent_angle += pi
1758        pos = points[-1][:2]
1759        self._add(
1760            pos,
1761            PathOps.ARC,
1762            (
1763                pos,
1764                tangent_angle,
1765                rx,
1766                ry,
1767                start_angle,
1768                signed_span,
1769                rot_angle,
1770                points,
1771            ),
1772            **kwargs,
1773        )
1774        return self
1775
1776    def sine(
1777        self,
1778        period: float = 40,
1779        amplitude: float = 20,
1780        duration: float = 40,
1781        phase_angle: float = 0,
1782        rot_angle: float = 0,
1783        damping: float = 0,
1784        n_points: int = 100,
1785        **kwargs: object,
1786    ) -> Self:
1787        """Append a sine-wave polyline from the current pen position.
1788
1789        Args:
1790            period: Wavelength. Defaults to 40.
1791            amplitude: Wave amplitude. Defaults to 20.
1792            duration: Horizontal length of the wave. Defaults to 40.
1793            phase_angle: Phase offset in radians. Defaults to 0.
1794            rot_angle: Rotation of the wave in radians. Defaults to 0.
1795            damping: Exponential damping factor. Defaults to 0.
1796            n_points: Number of samples. Defaults to 100.
1797            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1798
1799        Returns:
1800            Self: This path.
1801
1802        Examples:
1803            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1804            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).sine(period=20, amplitude=20, duration=20, n_points=4)
1805            >>> [round(float(c), 6) or 0.0 for c in p.pos[:2]]
1806            [20.0, 0.0]
1807            >>> [[round(float(c), 6) or 0.0 for c in q[:2]] for q in p.vertices]
1808            [[0.0, 0.0], [6.666667, 17.320508], [13.333333, -17.320508], [20.0, 0.0]]
1809"""
1810
1811        points = sine_points(
1812            period, amplitude, duration, n_points, phase_angle, damping
1813        )
1814        if rot_angle != 0:
1815            points = homogenize(points) @ rotation_matrix(rot_angle, points[0])
1816        points = homogenize(points) @ translation_matrix(*self.pos[:2])
1817        angle = line_angle(points[-2], points[-1])
1818        self._add(points[-1], PathOps.SINE, (points, angle), **kwargs)
1819        return self
1820
1821    def blend_sine(
1822        self,
1823        period: float = 40,
1824        amplitude: float = 20,
1825        duration: float = 40,
1826        phase_angle: float = 0,
1827        damping: float = 0,
1828        n_points: int = 100,
1829        **kwargs: object,
1830    ) -> Self:
1831        """Append a sine wave rotated to match the current heading.
1832
1833        Args:
1834            period: Wavelength. Defaults to 40.
1835            amplitude: Wave amplitude. Defaults to 20.
1836            duration: Horizontal length of the wave. Defaults to 40.
1837            phase_angle: Phase offset in radians. Defaults to 0.
1838            damping: Exponential damping factor. Defaults to 0.
1839            n_points: Number of samples. Defaults to 100.
1840            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1841
1842        Returns:
1843            Self: This path.
1844
1845        Examples:
1846            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1847            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=sg.pi / 4).blend_sine(duration=20, n_points=4)
1848            >>> [round(float(c), 5) for c in p.pos[:2]]
1849            [14.14214, 14.14214]
1850            >>> [[round(float(c), 6) for c in q[:2]] for q in p.vertices]
1851            [[0.0, 0.0], [14.142136, 14.142136]]
1852"""
1853
1854        points = sine_points(
1855            period, amplitude, duration, n_points, phase_angle, damping
1856        )
1857        start_angle = line_angle(points[0], points[1])
1858        rot_angle = self.angle - start_angle
1859        points = homogenize(points) @ rotation_matrix(rot_angle, points[0])
1860        points = homogenize(points) @ translation_matrix(*self.pos[:2])
1861        angle = line_angle(points[-2], points[-1])
1862        self._add(points[-1], PathOps.SINE, (points, angle), **kwargs)
1863        return self
1864
1865    def close(self, **kwargs: object) -> Self:
1866        """Close the current subpath back to its start.
1867
1868        Args:
1869            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1870
1871        Returns:
1872            Self: This path.
1873
1874        Examples:
1875            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1876            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 0)).line_to((40, 40)).close()
1877            >>> p.closed
1878            True
1879            >>> [[round(c, 6) for c in q[:2]] for q in p[-1].vertices]
1880            [[0.0, 0.0], [40.0, 0.0], [40.0, 40.0]]
1881"""
1882        self.closed = True
1883        self._add(self.pos, PathOps.CLOSE, None, **kwargs)
1884        return self
1885
1886    @property
1887    def vertices(self) -> list[PointType]:
1888        """Return deduplicated vertices from the path objects.
1889
1890        Returns:
1891            list: Path vertices in drawing order.
1892
1893        Examples:
1894            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1895            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((20, 0)).line_to((20, 20))
1896            >>> [[round(c, 6) for c in q[:2]] for q in p.vertices]
1897            [[0.0, 0.0], [20.0, 0.0], [20.0, 20.0]]
1898"""
1899        vertices = []
1900        last_vert = None
1901        abs_tol2 = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"] ** 2
1902        for obj in self.objects:
1903            if obj is not None and obj.vertices:
1904                obj_verts = obj.vertices
1905                if last_vert:
1906                    if close_points_square(last_vert, obj_verts[0], abs_tol2):
1907                        vertices.extend(obj_verts[1:])
1908                    else:
1909                        vertices.extend(obj_verts)
1910                else:
1911                    vertices.extend(obj_verts)
1912                last_vert = obj_verts[-1]
1913
1914        return vertices
1915
1916    def _label_vertices(self) -> list[PointType]:
1917        """Return vertices suitable for index / coordinate labels.
1918
1919        Line and polyline segments keep all corners. Sampled curves (arcs,
1920        Beziers, Hobby, sine) contribute only their first and last points so
1921        dense ellipse samples are not labeled.
1922
1923        Returns:
1924            list: Deduplicated landmark vertices in drawing order.
1925        """
1926        if len(self.objects) != len(self.operations):
1927            raise ValueError(
1928                "Path2D.objects and Path2D.operations length mismatch"
1929            )
1930
1931        vertices = []
1932        last_vert = None
1933        abs_tol2 = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"] ** 2
1934        for obj, operation in zip(self.objects, self.operations):
1935            if obj is None or not obj.vertices:
1936                continue
1937            obj_verts = obj.vertices
1938            if operation.subtype in _CURVE_PATH_OPS and len(obj_verts) > 2:
1939                obj_verts = [obj_verts[0], obj_verts[-1]]
1940            if last_vert:
1941                if close_points_square(last_vert, obj_verts[0], abs_tol2):
1942                    vertices.extend(obj_verts[1:])
1943                else:
1944                    vertices.extend(obj_verts)
1945            else:
1946                vertices.extend(obj_verts)
1947            last_vert = obj_verts[-1]
1948
1949        return vertices
1950
1951    def set_style(
1952        self, name: str, value: object, **kwargs: object
1953    ) -> Self:
1954        """Record a style change in the path operation list.
1955
1956        Args:
1957            name: Style attribute name.
1958            value: Style value.
1959            **kwargs: Extra style metadata.
1960
1961        Returns:
1962            Self: This path.
1963
1964        Note:
1965            The example is skipped because ``PathOperation`` has no ``STYLE``
1966            member, so ``set_style`` currently raises ``AttributeError``.
1967
1968        Examples:
1969            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1970            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).set_style("line_width", 2)  # doctest: +SKIP
1971            >>> p.operations[-1][1][0]  # doctest: +SKIP
1972            'line_width'
1973"""
1974        self.operations.append((PathOps.STYLE, (name, value, kwargs)))
1975        return self
1976
1977    def _update(
1978        self,
1979        xform_matrix: NDArray,
1980        reps: int = 0,
1981        take: slice | None = None,
1982        incr: float
1983        | tuple[float, float]
1984        | tuple[callable, Any]
1985        | tuple[InPlace, Any]
1986        | NDArray
1987        | Sequence[Sequence[float]]
1988        | None = None,
1989        dyn_ref: Callable | None = None,
1990        merge: bool = False,
1991        xform_type: TransformationType = None,
1992    ) -> Group:
1993        """Apply a transform to this path, optionally repeating it.
1994
1995        Args:
1996            xform_matrix: 3x3 affine matrix.
1997            reps: Extra copies to generate. Defaults to 0.
1998            take: Not supported; must be ``None``.
1999            incr: Increment applied between repetitions when ``reps > 0``.
2000            dyn_ref: Matrix factory built by the transform method when
2001                dynamic references are in use. Defaults to None.
2002            merge: If True and ``reps > 0``, merge resulting shapes.
2003            xform_type: Transform kind used with ``incr``.
2004
2005        Returns:
2006            Group: ``self`` when ``reps == 0``, otherwise a group of copies.
2007
2008        Raises:
2009            ValueError: If ``take`` is set.
2010        """
2011        if take is not None:
2012            raise ValueError(
2013                "Path2D._update does not support take=; transform the whole path."
2014            )
2015        if reps == 0:
2016            original_pos = self.pos
2017            direction_point = (
2018                original_pos[0] + cos(self.angle),
2019                original_pos[1] + sin(self.angle),
2020            )
2021            self.start = _transform_path_point(self.start, xform_matrix)
2022            self.pos = _transform_path_point(self.pos, xform_matrix)
2023            self.angle = line_angle(
2024                _transform_path_point(original_pos, xform_matrix),
2025                _transform_path_point(direction_point, xform_matrix),
2026            )
2027            self.operations = [
2028                _transform_path_operation(operation, xform_matrix)
2029                for operation in self.operations
2030            ]
2031            self.handles = [
2032                _transform_path_points(handle, xform_matrix)
2033                for handle in self.handles
2034            ]
2035            for obj in self.objects:
2036                if obj is not None:
2037                    obj._update(xform_matrix)
2038
2039            # Check this!!!!
2040            for element in self.elements:
2041                if element is not None and element.type == Types.SHAPE:
2042                    element._update(xform_matrix)
2043            res = self
2044        else:
2045            paths = [self]
2046            path = self
2047            if dyn_ref:
2048                pattern = Group()
2049                pattern.elements = paths
2050                targets = _Targets(self, pattern)
2051            else:
2052                targets = None
2053            for i in range(reps):
2054                path = path.copy()
2055                if targets is not None:
2056                    targets.active = path
2057                xform_matrix = _next_xform_matrix(
2058                    xform_matrix, xform_type, incr, dyn_ref, targets, i
2059                )
2060                path._update(xform_matrix)
2061                paths.append(path)
2062            res = Group(paths)
2063        if merge and reps > 0:
2064            res = res.merge_shapes()
2065        return res

Constructive 2D path with a pen position and heading.

Operations such as line_to, cubic_to, and arc append geometry while updating pos and angle. The path is also a Group of Shape segments for transforms and drawing.

color sets both line_color and fill_color. alpha sets both line_alpha and fill_alpha. Reading an unset line_color / fill_color / line_alpha / fill_alpha returns the matching configured default. Style color/alpha and copy_style come from CommonStyle.

Attributes:
  • pos: Current pen position.
  • start: Path start point.
  • angle: Current heading in radians.
  • operations: List of Operation records.
  • subtype: Types.PATH2D.
Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> path = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=0)
>>> _ = path.forward(40).turn(sg.pi / 2).forward(20)
>>> round(path.pos[0], 6), round(path.pos[1], 6)
(40.0, 20.0)

def copy(self) -> Path2D: 
430    def copy(self) -> "Path2D":
431        """Return a deep-enough copy of the path for independent editing.
432
433        Returns:
434            Path2D: Copied path with cloned elements and operations.
435
436        Examples:
437            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
438            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 0))
439            >>> q = p.copy()
440            >>> _ = q.line_to((40, 20))
441            >>> len(p.operations), len(q.operations)
442            (1, 2)
443"""
444
445        new_path = Path2D(start=self.start)
446        cur_shape_index = None
447        for index, element in enumerate(self.elements):
448            if element is self.cur_shape:
449                cur_shape_index = index
450                break
451
452        new_path.pos = self.pos
453        new_path.angle = self.angle
454        new_path.operations = (
455            self.operations.copy()
456        )  # shallow-copy of list is fine if Operations are treated as immutable
457        new_path.elements = [element.copy() for element in self.elements]
458        new_path.objects = []
459        for obj in self.objects:
460            if obj is not None:
461                new_path.objects.append(obj.copy())
462            else:
463                new_path.objects.append(None)
464        new_path.even_odd = self.even_odd
465        new_path.closed = self.closed
466        if cur_shape_index is not None:
467            new_path.cur_shape = new_path.elements[cur_shape_index]
468        else:
469            new_path.cur_shape = self.cur_shape.copy()
470        new_path.handles = list(self.handles)
471        new_path.stack = deque(self.stack)
472        new_path.copy_style(self)
473        return new_path

def uniform_points( self, distance: float, align_section_ends: bool = True, align_path_end: bool = True, rel_tol: float | None = None, abs_tol: float | None = None) -> list[tuple[float, float]]: 
574    def uniform_points(
575        self,
576        distance: float,
577        align_section_ends: bool = True,
578        align_path_end: bool = True,
579        rel_tol: float | None = None,
580        abs_tol: float | None = None,
581    ) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
582        """Return points spaced by ``distance`` along the path.
583
584        Sampling restarts on each section. A section end is included when
585        the leftover stub is within tolerance of ``distance`` (or of 0),
586        or when the matching align flag is True. On the last section,
587        ``align_path_end`` is used instead of ``align_section_ends``.
588        Connected section starts are not repeated; a new subpath start is.
589
590        Args:
591            distance: Arc-length spacing. Must be positive.
592            align_section_ends: If True, always include each non-final
593                section end. Defaults to True.
594            align_path_end: If True, always include the path end.
595                Defaults to True.
596            rel_tol: Relative leftover tolerance. ``None`` uses
597                ``runtime_defaults["rel_tol"]``.
598            abs_tol: Absolute leftover tolerance. ``None`` uses
599                ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
600
601        Returns:
602            list[tuple[float, float]]: Sample points in path order.
603
604        Raises:
605            ValueError: If ``distance`` is not positive.
606
607        Examples:
608            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
609            >>> path = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 0))
610            >>> path.uniform_points(20)
611            [(0.0, 0.0), (20.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0)]
612            >>> path.uniform_points(20, align_path_end=False)
613            [(0.0, 0.0), (20.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0)]
614            >>> corner = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 0)).line_to((40, 20))
615            >>> corner.uniform_points(20)
616            [(0.0, 0.0), (20.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 20.0)]
617            >>> corner.uniform_points(20, align_section_ends=False)
618            [(0.0, 0.0), (20.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 20.0)]
619            >>> path.uniform_points(20, True, True, 0, 0.001)[-1]
620            (40.0, 0.0)
621            >>> path.uniform_points(0)
622            Traceback (most recent call last):
623                ...
624            ValueError: distance must be positive
625        """
626        if distance <= 0:
627            raise ValueError("distance must be positive")
628        rel_tol, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
629        abs_tol2 = abs_tol * abs_tol
630
631        def lengths_close(first: float, second: float) -> bool:
632            return bool(
633                np.isclose(first, second, rtol=rel_tol, atol=abs_tol)
634            )
635
636        def append_unique(
637            points: list[tuple[float, float]], point: PointType
638        ) -> None:
639            xy = _xy_point(point)
640            if points and close_points_square(points[-1], xy, abs_tol2):
641                return
642            points.append(xy)
643
644        points: list[tuple[float, float]] = []
645        previous_end: tuple[float, float] | None = None
646        sections = self.sections
647        last_index = len(sections) - 1
648        for index, section in enumerate(sections):
649            vertices = list(section.vertices)
650            if not vertices:
651                continue
652            start = _xy_point(vertices[0])
653            end = _xy_point(vertices[-1])
654            connected = previous_end is not None and close_points_square(
655                previous_end, start, abs_tol2
656            )
657            if not connected:
658                append_unique(points, start)
659            if len(vertices) < 2:
660                previous_end = end
661                continue
662            section_length = polyline_length(
663                vertices, closed=False, abs_tol=abs_tol
664            )
665            last_s = 0.0
666            while True:
667                next_s = last_s + distance
668                if next_s > section_length or lengths_close(
669                    next_s, section_length
670                ):
671                    break
672                append_unique(
673                    points, _polyline_point_at_length(vertices, next_s)
674                )
675                last_s = next_s
676            leftover = section_length - last_s
677            align_end = (
678                align_path_end if index == last_index else align_section_ends
679            )
680            if lengths_close(leftover, 0.0):
681                pass
682            elif lengths_close(leftover, distance) or align_end:
683                append_unique(points, end)
684            previous_end = end
685        return points

Return points spaced by distance along the path.

def pop(self) -> None: 
717    def pop(self) -> None:
718        """Restore the pen position and heading from the stack.
719
720        Starts a new subpath at the restored position so later drawing is
721        not connected to the segment that was drawn after ``push``. Does
722        nothing if the stack is empty.
723
724        Examples:
725            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
726            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=0)
727            >>> p.push()
728            >>> _ = p.forward(20).turn(sg.pi / 2)
729            >>> p.pop()
730            >>> p.angle
731            0
732            >>> p.pos
733            (0, 0)
734"""
735        if not self.stack:
736            return
737        pos, angle = self.stack.pop()
738        self.operations.append(Operation(PathOps.MOVE_TO, pos))
739        self._create_object()
740        self.pos = pos
741        self.angle = angle

Restore the pen position and heading from the stack.

Starts a new subpath at the restored position so later drawing is not connected to the segment that was drawn after push. Does nothing if the stack is empty.

Examples:
