>>> p.push()
>>> _ = p.forward(20).turn(sg.pi / 2)
>>> p.pop()
>>> p.angle
0
>>> p.pos
(0, 0)
def r_coord(self, dx: float, dy: float) -> Sequence[float]: 
743    def r_coord(self, dx: float, dy: float) -> PointType:
744        """Map local offsets into world coordinates relative to the pen.
745
746        The local y-axis is aligned with the current heading.
747
748        Args:
749            dx: Offset along the local x-axis.
750            dy: Offset along the local y-axis (heading direction).
751
752        Returns:
753            PointType: Absolute point.
754
755        Examples:
756            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
757            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=sg.pi / 2)
758            >>> x, y = p.r_coord(0, 40)
759            >>> round(x, 6), round(y, 6)
760            (0.0, 40.0)
761"""
762        x, y = self.pos[:2]
763        theta = self.angle - pi / 2
764        x1 = dx * cos(theta) - dy * sin(theta) + x
765        y1 = dx * sin(theta) + dy * cos(theta) + y
766
767        return x1, y1

769    def r_polar(self, r: float, angle: float) -> PointType:
770        """Return an absolute point from polar offsets relative to the pen.
771
772        Angle ``0`` is aligned with the current heading.
773
774        Args:
775            r: Radius.
776            angle: Angle in radians relative to the heading.
777
778        Returns:
779            PointType: Absolute point.

782            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg

787"""
788        x, y = polar_to_cartesian(r, angle + self.angle - pi / 2)[:2]
789        x1, y1 = self.pos[:2]
790
791        return x1 + x, y1 + y

def move( self, pos: Sequence[float], anchor: simetri.base.all_enums.Anchor = <Anchor.CENTER: 'center'>, **kwargs: object) -> Self: 
877    def move(
878        self,
879        pos: PointType,
880        anchor: Anchor = Anchor.CENTER,
881        **kwargs: object,
882    ) -> Self:
883        """Translate the whole path so a bbox anchor sits at ``pos``.
884
885        Args:
886            pos: Target location for the chosen anchor.
887            anchor: Bounding-box anchor (default ``Anchor.CENTER``).
888            **kwargs: Extra attributes set on the path before transforming.
889
890        Returns:
891            Self or Group: Transformed path (or group when repetitions apply).
892
893        Examples:
894            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
895            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 0))
896            >>> _ = p.move((50, 50))
897            >>> abs(p.b_box.center[0] - 50) < 1e-6
898            True
899"""
900        x, y = pos[:2]
901        anchor = get_enum_value(Anchor, anchor)
902        x1, y1 = getattr(self.b_box, anchor)
903        transform = translation_matrix(x - x1, y - y1)
904        for k, v in kwargs.items():
905            setattr(self, k, v)
906        res = self._update(transform, reps=0)
907
908        return res

def r_segments(self, r_points: Sequence[Sequence[float]], **kwargs: object) -> Self: 
1145    def r_segments(
1146        self, r_points: Sequence[PointType], **kwargs: object
1147    ) -> Self:
1148        """Append polyline segments using successive ``(dx, dy)`` offsets.
1149
1150        Args:
1151            r_points: Sequence of relative offsets.
1152            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1153
1154        Returns:
1155            Self: This path.
1156
1157        Examples:
1158            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1159            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).r_segments([(20, 0), (0, 20)])
1160            >>> p.pos
1161            (20, 20)
1162"""
1163        # Convert relative offsets to absolute points
1164        points = []
1165        current_x, current_y = self.pos
1166        for dx, dy in r_points:
1167            current_x += dx
1168            current_y += dy
1169            points.append((current_x, current_y))

1213        """Append a quadratic Bézier to ``end`` with control point ``control``.
1214

1216

1218            control: Control point.

1226        Raises:

1231            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0)).quad_to((20, 20), (40, 0))
1232            >>> p.pos

1237            PathOps.QUAD_TO,
1238            (self.pos[:2], control, end[:2]),

1241        )
1242        pos = end
1243        for arg in args:
1244            if len(arg) != 2:
1245                raise ValueError("Invalid number of arguments for curve.")
1246            if isinstance(arg[0], (int, float)):
1247                # (length, end)
1248                length = arg[0]
1249                control = extended_line(length, control, pos)
1250                end = arg[1]

1252                    end, PathOps.QUAD_TO, (pos, control, end), pnt2=control
1253                )

1256                # (control, end)
1257                control = arg[0]
1258                end = arg[1]
1259                self._add(
1260                    end, PathOps.QUAD_TO, (pos, control, end), pnt2=control
1261                )
1262                pos = end
1263        return self

1292    def mirror_cubic_to(
1293        self, control2: PointType, end: PointType, **kwargs: object
1294    ) -> Self:
1295        """Append a smooth cubic Bézier (SVG ``S``).
1296
1297        Mirrors the previous second control point across the current position
1298        to obtain the first control point.
1299
1300        Args:
1301            control2: Second control point.
1302            end: Curve end point.
1303            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1304
1305        Returns:
1306            Self: This path.
1307
1308        Examples:
1309            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1310            >>> p = (
1311            ... sg.Path2D((0, 0))
1312            ... .cubic_to((40, 80), (60, 80), (80, 0))
1313            ... .mirror_cubic_to((20, -80), (80, 0))
1314            ... )
1315            >>> p.pos
1316            (80, 0)
1317"""
1318        # Get previous control point from last operation if it was a cubic
1319        prev_c2 = self.pos
1320        last_op = self.operations[-1] if self.operations else None
1321        if last_op and last_op.subtype in _CUBIC_PATH_OPS:
1322            # data: (start, c1, c2, end)
1323            prev_c2 = last_op.data[2]
1324
1325        # Mirror prev_c2 across current position
1326        cur_x, cur_y = self.pos
1327        c1_x = 2 * cur_x - prev_c2[0]
1328        c1_y = 2 * cur_y - prev_c2[1]
1329        control1 = (c1_x, c1_y)
1330
1331        self._add(
1332            end,
1333            PathOps.CUBIC_TO,
1334            (self.pos, control1, control2, end),
1335            pnt2=control2,
1336            **kwargs,
1337        )
1338        return self

@alias_argument({'radius_x': 'rx', 'radius_y': 'ry'})
def arc( self, radius_x: float, radius_y: float | None = None, start_angle: float = 0, span_angle: float | None = None, rot_angle: float = 0, n_points: int | None = None, *, end_angle: float | None = None, clockwise: bool = False, **kwargs: object) -> Self: 
1486    @alias_argument({"radius_x": "rx", "radius_y": "ry"})
1487    def arc(
1488        self,
1489        radius_x: float,
1490        radius_y: float | None = None,
1491        start_angle: float = 0,
1492        span_angle: float | None = None,
1493        rot_angle: float = 0,
1494        n_points: int | None = None,
1495        *,
1496        end_angle: float | None = None,
1497        clockwise: bool = False,
1498        **kwargs: object,
1499    ) -> Self:
1500        """Append an elliptic arc starting at the current pen position.
1501
1502        Pass either ``span_angle`` or ``end_angle``, not both. Use
1503        ``clockwise=True`` or a negative ``span_angle`` for a clockwise
1504        arc.
1505
1506        Args:
1507            radius_x: Ellipse half-width.
1508            radius_y: Ellipse half-height; defaults to ``radius_x``.
1509            start_angle: Arc start angle in radians. Defaults to 0.
1510            span_angle: Sweep in radians. A negative value draws clockwise.
1511                Mutually exclusive with ``end_angle``. At least one of
1512                ``span_angle`` or ``end_angle`` is required.
1513            rot_angle: Ellipse rotation in radians. Defaults to 0.
1514            n_points: Sample count; defaults to ``runtime_defaults['n_arc_points']``.
1515            end_angle: Ending angle in radians. Mutually exclusive with
1516                ``span_angle``.
1517            clockwise: If True, the arc is drawn clockwise. Defaults to False.
1518            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1519
1520        Returns:
1521            Self: This path.
1522
1523        Examples:
1524            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1525            >>> p = sg.Path2D((40, 0), angle=0).arc(40, 40, 0, sg.pi / 2)
1526            >>> round(float(p.pos[0]), 5), round(float(p.pos[1]), 5)
1527            (0.0, 40.0)
1528            >>> p = sg.Path2D((40, 0), angle=0).arc(40, 40, 0, -sg.pi / 2)
1529            >>> round(float(p.pos[0]), 5) or 0.0, round(float(p.pos[1]), 5)
1530            (0.0, -40.0)
1531"""
1532        if radius_y is None:
1533            radius_y = radius_x
1534        rx = radius_x
1535        ry = radius_y
1536        start_angle = positive_angle(start_angle)
1537        signed_span = resolve_arc_sweep(
1538            start_angle, span_angle, end_angle, clockwise
1539        )
1540        clockwise = signed_span < 0
1541        if n_points is None:
1542            n_points = runtime_defaults["n_arc_points"]
1543        points = _elliptic_arc_points_from_signed(
1544            (0, 0), rx, ry, start_angle, signed_span, n_points
1545        )
1546        start = points[0]
1547        end = points[-1]
1548        # Translate the start to the current position and rotate by the rotation angle.
1549        dx = self.pos[0] - start[0]
1550        dy = self.pos[1] - start[1]
1551        rotocenter = start
1552        if rot_angle != 0:
1553            points = (
1554                homogenize(points)
1555                @ rotation_matrix(rot_angle, rotocenter)
1556                @ translation_matrix(dx, dy)
1557            )
1558        else:
1559            points = homogenize(points) @ translation_matrix(dx, dy)
1560        tangent_angle = ellipse_tangent(rx, ry, *end) + rot_angle
1561        if clockwise:
1562            tangent_angle += pi
1563        pos = points[-1]
1564        self._add(
1565            pos,
1566            PathOps.ARC,
1567            (
1568                pos,
1569                tangent_angle,
1570                rx,
1571                ry,
1572                start_angle,
1573                signed_span,
1574                rot_angle,
1575                points,
1576            ),
1577            **kwargs,
1578        )
1579        return self

Append an elliptic arc starting at the current pen position.

Pass either span_angle or end_angle, not both. Use clockwise=True or a negative span_angle for a clockwise arc.

  • rot_angle: Ellipse rotation in radians. Defaults to 0.
  • n_points: Sample count; defaults to runtime_defaults['n_arc_points'].
  • end_angle: Ending angle in radians. Mutually exclusive with span_angle.

1680    def blend_arc(
1681        self,
1682        radius_x: float,

1684        start_angle: float = 0,
1685        span_angle: float | None = None,
1686        sharp: bool = False,
1687        n_points: int | None = None,
1688        *,
1689        end_angle: float | None = None,
1690        clockwise: bool = False,
1691        **kwargs: object,
1692    ) -> Self:
1693        """Append an elliptic arc blended to the current heading.
1694
1695        Pass either ``span_angle`` or ``end_angle``, not both. Use
1696        ``clockwise=True`` or a negative ``span_angle`` for a clockwise
1697        arc.
1698
1699        Args:
1700            radius_x: Ellipse half-width.
1701            radius_y: Ellipse half-height; defaults to ``radius_x``.
1702            start_angle: Arc start angle in radians. Defaults to 0.
1703            span_angle: Sweep in radians. A negative value draws clockwise.
1704                Mutually exclusive with ``end_angle``. At least one of
1705                ``span_angle`` or ``end_angle`` is required.
1706            sharp: Flip the blend orientation if True. Defaults to False.
1707            n_points: Sample count; defaults to ``runtime_defaults['n_arc_points']``.
1708            end_angle: Ending angle in radians. Mutually exclusive with
1709                ``span_angle``.
1710            clockwise: If True, the arc is drawn clockwise. Defaults to False.
1711            **kwargs: Style overrides applied to the segment. ``name`` labels the operation.
1712
1713        Returns:
1714            Self: This path.
1715
1716        Examples:
1717            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1718            >>> p = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=0).blend_arc(40, 40, 0, sg.pi / 2)
1719            >>> [round(float(c), 5) for c in p.pos[:2]]
1720            [40.0, 40.0]
1721            >>> [round(float(c), 5) for c in p.vertices[0][:2]], [round(float(c), 5) for c in p.vertices[-1][:2]]
1722            ([0.0, 0.0], [40.0, 40.0])
1723"""
1724        if radius_y is None:
1725            radius_y = radius_x
1726        rx = radius_x
1727        ry = radius_y
1728        start_angle = positive_angle(start_angle)
1729        signed_span = resolve_arc_sweep(
1730            start_angle, span_angle, end_angle, clockwise
1731        )
1732        clockwise = signed_span < 0
1733        if n_points is None:
1734            n_points = runtime_defaults["n_arc_points"]
1735        points = _elliptic_arc_points_from_signed(
1736            (0, 0), rx, ry, start_angle, signed_span, n_points
1737        )
1738        start = points[0]
1739        end = points[-1]
1740        # Translate the start to the current position and rotate by the computed rotation angle.
1741        dx = self.pos[0] - start[0]
1742        dy = self.pos[1] - start[1]
1743        rotocenter = start
1744        tangent = ellipse_tangent(rx, ry, *start)
1745        rot_angle = self.angle - tangent
1746        if clockwise:
1747            rot_angle += pi
1748        if sharp:
1749            rot_angle += pi
1750        points = (
1751            homogenize(points)
1752            @ rotation_matrix(rot_angle, rotocenter)
1753            @ translation_matrix(dx, dy)
1754        )

1756        if clockwise:
1757            tangent_angle += pi
1758        pos = points[-1][:2]
1759        self._add(
1760            pos,
1761            PathOps.ARC,
1762            (
1763                pos,
1764                tangent_angle,
1765                rx,
1766                ry,
1767                start_angle,
1768                signed_span,
1769                rot_angle,
1770                points,
1771            ),
1772            **kwargs,
1773        )
1774        return self

2165    """Return the SVG path ``d`` string for a ``Path2D``.
2166
2167    Args:
2168        path2d: Path to convert.
2169
2170    Returns:
2171        str: SVG path data.
2172
2173    Examples:
2174        >>> d = path2d_to_svg_path(sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 0)))
2175        >>> d.startswith("M")
2176        True
2177    """

2180        """Format a float to a string with 3 decimal places."""
2181        return f"{val:.3f}".rstrip("0").rstrip(".")
2182
2183    parts = [f"M {fmt(path2d.start[0])},{fmt(path2d.start[1])}"]
2184
2185    obj_idx = 0
2186    PO = PathOps
2187
2188    for op in path2d.operations:
2189        if isinstance(op, tuple):
2190            continue
2191
2192        st = op.subtype
2193        data = op.data
2194
2195        current_obj = (
2196            path2d.objects[obj_idx]
2197            if obj_idx < len(path2d.objects)
2198            else None
2199        )
2200
2201        if st in _MOVE_PATH_OPS:
2202            parts.append(f"M {fmt(data[0])},{fmt(data[1])}")
2203
2204        elif st in _LINE_PATH_OPS:
2205            end = data[1]
2206            parts.append(f"L {fmt(end[0])},{fmt(end[1])}")
2207
2208        elif st == PO.SEGMENTS:
2209            parts.extend(f"L {fmt(p[0])},{fmt(p[1])}" for p in data[1])
2210
2211        elif st in _CUBIC_PATH_OPS:
2212            c1, c2, end = data[1], data[2], data[3]
2213            parts.append(
2214                f"C {fmt(c1[0])},{fmt(c1[1])} {fmt(c2[0])},{fmt(c2[1])} {fmt(end[0])},{fmt(end[1])}"
2215            )
2216
2217        elif st in _QUAD_PATH_OPS:
2218            c1, end = data[1], data[2]
2219            parts.append(
2220                f"Q {fmt(c1[0])},{fmt(c1[1])} {fmt(end[0])},{fmt(end[1])}"
2221            )
2222
2223        elif st in _ARC_PATH_OPS:
2224            rx, ry = data[2], data[3]
2225            span = data[5]
2226            rot = degrees(data[6])
2227            points = data[7]
2228            end = points[-1]
2229            large_arc = 1 if abs(span) > pi else 0
2230            sweep = 1 if span > 0 else 0
2231            parts.append(
2232                f"A {fmt(rx)} {fmt(ry)} {fmt(rot)} {large_arc} {sweep} {fmt(end[0])},{fmt(end[1])}"
2233            )
2234
2235        elif st == PO.CLOSE:
2236            parts.append("Z")
2237
2238        elif st in _SINE_PATH_OPS:
2239            parts.extend(f"L {fmt(p[0])},{fmt(p[1])}" for p in data[0])
2240
2241        elif st == PO.HOBBY_TO and current_obj:
2242            verts = current_obj.vertices
2243            parts.extend(f"L {fmt(p[0])},{fmt(p[1])}" for p in verts[1:])
2244
2245        obj_idx += 1
2246
2247    return " ".join(parts)

str: SVG path data.

2164def path2d_to_svg_path(path2d: Path2D) -> str:
2165    """Return the SVG path ``d`` string for a ``Path2D``.
2166
2167    Args:
2168        path2d: Path to convert.
2169
2170    Returns:
2171        str: SVG path data.
2172
2173    Examples:
2174        >>> d = path2d_to_svg_path(sg.Path2D((0, 0)).line_to((40, 0)))
2175        >>> d.startswith("M")
2176        True
2177    """
2178
2179    def fmt(val: float) -> str:
2180        """Format a float to a string with 3 decimal places."""
2181        return f"{val:.3f}".rstrip("0").rstrip(".")
2182
2183    parts = [f"M {fmt(path2d.start[0])},{fmt(path2d.start[1])}"]
2184
2185    obj_idx = 0
2186    PO = PathOps
2187
2188    for op in path2d.operations:
2189        if isinstance(op, tuple):
2190            continue
2191
2192        st = op.subtype
2193        data = op.data
2194
2195        current_obj = (
2196            path2d.objects[obj_idx]
2197            if obj_idx < len(path2d.objects)
2198            else None
2199        )
2200
2201        if st in _MOVE_PATH_OPS:
2202            parts.append(f"M {fmt(data[0])},{fmt(data[1])}")
2203
2204        elif st in _LINE_PATH_OPS:
2205            end = data[1]
2206            parts.append(f"L {fmt(end[0])},{fmt(end[1])}")
2207
2208        elif st == PO.SEGMENTS:
2209            parts.extend(f"L {fmt(p[0])},{fmt(p[1])}" for p in data[1])
2210
2211        elif st in _CUBIC_PATH_OPS:
2212            c1, c2, end = data[1], data[2], data[3]
2213            parts.append(
2214                f"C {fmt(c1[0])},{fmt(c1[1])} {fmt(c2[0])},{fmt(c2[1])} {fmt(end[0])},{fmt(end[1])}"
2215            )
2216
2217        elif st in _QUAD_PATH_OPS:
2218            c1, end = data[1], data[2]
2219            parts.append(
2220                f"Q {fmt(c1[0])},{fmt(c1[1])} {fmt(end[0])},{fmt(end[1])}"
2221            )
2222
2223        elif st in _ARC_PATH_OPS:
2224            rx, ry = data[2], data[3]
2225            span = data[5]
2226            rot = degrees(data[6])
2227            points = data[7]
2228            end = points[-1]
2229            large_arc = 1 if abs(span) > pi else 0
2230            sweep = 1 if span > 0 else 0
2231            parts.append(
2232                f"A {fmt(rx)} {fmt(ry)} {fmt(rot)} {large_arc} {sweep} {fmt(end[0])},{fmt(end[1])}"
2233            )
2234
2235        elif st == PO.CLOSE:
2236            parts.append("Z")
2237
2238        elif st in _SINE_PATH_OPS:
2239            parts.extend(f"L {fmt(p[0])},{fmt(p[1])}" for p in data[0])
2240
2241        elif st == PO.HOBBY_TO and current_obj:
2242            verts = current_obj.vertices
2243            parts.extend(f"L {fmt(p[0])},{fmt(p[1])}" for p in verts[1:])
2244
2245        obj_idx += 1
2246
2247    return " ".join(parts)

def path_code( path2d: Path2D, n_round: int | None = None) -> str: 
2318def path_code(path2d: Path2D, n_round: int | None = None) -> str:
2319    """Return Python source that reconstructs ``path2d``.
2320
2321    The snippet assumes ``import simetri.graphics as sg``. Geometry comes from
2322    ``path2d.start``, ``path2d.angle``, and ``path2d.operations``. ``turn``,
2323    ``orient``, ``push``, and ``pop`` are not stored; ``forward`` is emitted as
2324    ``line_to`` so the replay does not depend on a lost heading.
2325
2326    Args:
2327        path2d: Path to serialize.
2328        n_round: Decimal places for coordinates and lengths derived from them.
2329            ``None`` uses ``runtime_defaults['n_round']``.
2330
2331    Returns:
2332        Python source that builds an equivalent ``Path2D``.
2333
2334    Raises:
2335        ValueError: If an operation subtype has no code mapping, or
2336            ``n_round`` is negative.
2337        TypeError: If a style value cannot be serialized.
2338
2339    Examples:
2340        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2341        >>> sample = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=0).line_to((40, 0)).close()
2342        >>> print(sg.path_code(sample))
2343        path = sg.Path2D(start=(0, 0), angle=0)
2344        path.line_to((40, 0))
2345        path.close()
2346        >>> messy = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=0).line_to((10.126, 0))
2347        >>> print(sg.path_code(messy, n_round=2))
2348        path = sg.Path2D(start=(0, 0), angle=0)
2349        path.line_to((10.13, 0))
2350    """
2351    if n_round is None:
2352        n_round = runtime_defaults["n_round"]
2353    if n_round < 0:
2354        raise ValueError("n_round must be a nonnegative integer.")
2355    start_x, start_y = path2d.start[:2]
2356    lines = [
2357        (
2358            "path = sg.Path2D("
2359            f"start={_format_path_code_point((start_x, start_y), n_round)}, "
2360            f"angle={_format_path_code_number(path2d.angle)}"
2361            ")"
2362        )
2363    ]
2364
2365    for operation in path2d.operations:
2366        if isinstance(operation, tuple):
2367            _opcode, payload = operation
2368            name, value, style_kwargs = payload
2369            arguments = [
2370                _format_path_code_value(name),
2371                _format_path_code_value(value),
2372            ]
2373            for key, style_value in style_kwargs.items():
2374                arguments.append(
2375                    f"{key}={_format_path_code_value(style_value)}"
2376                )
2377            lines.append(_format_path_code_call("set_style", *arguments))
2378            continue
2379
2380        subtype = operation.subtype
2381        data = operation.data
2382
2383        if subtype in _LINE_TO_FORWARD_OPS:
2384            _start, end = data
2385            lines.append(
2386                _format_path_code_call(
2387                    "line_to", _format_path_code_point(end, n_round)
2388                )
2389            )
2390        elif subtype in _MOVE_PATH_OPS:
2391            lines.append(
2392                _format_path_code_call(
2393                    "move_to", _format_path_code_point(data, n_round)
2394                )
2395            )
2396        elif subtype == PathOps.R_LINE:
2397            start_point, end_point = data
2398            start_x, start_y = start_point[:2]
2399            end_x, end_y = end_point[:2]
2400            lines.append(
2401                _format_path_code_call(
2402                    "r_line",
2403                    _format_path_code_number(end_x - start_x, n_round),
2404                    _format_path_code_number(end_y - start_y, n_round),
2405                )
2406            )
2407        elif subtype == PathOps.H_LINE_TO:
2408            _start, end_point = data
2409            end_x, _end_y = end_point[:2]
2410            lines.append(
2411                _format_path_code_call(
2412                    "h_line_to", _format_path_code_number(end_x, n_round)
2413                )
2414            )
2415        elif subtype == PathOps.R_H_LINE:
2416            start_point, end_point = data
2417            start_x, _start_y = start_point[:2]
2418            end_x, _end_y = end_point[:2]
2419            lines.append(
2420                _format_path_code_call(
2421                    "r_h_line",
2422                    _format_path_code_number(end_x - start_x, n_round),
2423                )
2424            )
2425        elif subtype == PathOps.V_LINE_TO:
2426            _start, end_point = data
2427            _end_x, end_y = end_point[:2]
2428            lines.append(
2429                _format_path_code_call(
2430                    "v_line_to", _format_path_code_number(end_y, n_round)
2431                )
2432            )
2433        elif subtype == PathOps.R_V_LINE:
2434            start_point, end_point = data
2435            _start_x, start_y = start_point[:2]
2436            _end_x, end_y = end_point[:2]
2437            lines.append(
2438                _format_path_code_call(
2439                    "r_v_line",
2440                    _format_path_code_number(end_y - start_y, n_round),
2441                )
2442            )
2443        elif subtype == PathOps.SEGMENTS:
2444            _start, points = data
2445            lines.append(
2446                _format_path_code_call(
2447                    "segments", _format_path_code_points(points, n_round)
2448                )
2449            )
2450        elif subtype in _CUBIC_PATH_OPS:
2451            _start, control1, control2, end = data
2452            lines.append(
2453                _format_path_code_call(
2454                    "cubic_to",
2455                    _format_path_code_point(control1, n_round),
2456                    _format_path_code_point(control2, n_round),
2457                    _format_path_code_point(end, n_round),
2458                )
2459            )
2460        elif subtype in _QUAD_PATH_OPS:
2461            _start, control, end = data
2462            lines.append(
2463                _format_path_code_call(
2464                    "quad_to",
2465                    _format_path_code_point(control, n_round),
2466                    _format_path_code_point(end, n_round),
2467                )
2468            )
2469        elif subtype == PathOps.HOBBY_TO:
2470            _start, points = data
2471            lines.append(
2472                _format_path_code_call(
2473                    "hobby_to", _format_path_code_points(points, n_round)
2474                )
2475            )
2476        elif subtype in _ARC_CODE_PATH_OPS:
2477            (
2478                _end,
2479                _tangent_angle,
2480                radius_x,
2481                radius_y,
2482                start_angle,
2483                span_angle,
2484                rot_angle,
2485                _points,
2486            ) = data
2487            arguments = [
2488                _format_path_code_number(radius_x, n_round),
2489                _format_path_code_number(radius_y, n_round),
2490                _format_path_code_number(start_angle),
2491                _format_path_code_number(abs(span_angle)),
2492            ]
2493            if span_angle < 0:
2494                arguments.append("clockwise=True")
2495            if rot_angle != 0:
2496                arguments.append(
2497                    f"rot_angle={_format_path_code_number(rot_angle)}"
2498                )
2499            lines.append(_format_path_code_call("arc", *arguments))
2500        elif subtype in _SINE_PATH_OPS:
2501            points, _angle = data
2502            remaining = list(points[1:])
2503            lines.append(
2504                _format_path_code_call(
2505                    "segments", _format_path_code_points(remaining, n_round)
2506                )
2507            )
2508        elif subtype == PathOps.CLOSE:
2509            lines.append("path.close()")
2510        else:
2511            raise ValueError(
2512                f"Cannot generate path code for operation {subtype!r}"
2513            )
2514
2515    return "\n".join(lines)

Return Python source that reconstructs path2d.

The snippet assumes import simetri.graphics as sg. Geometry comes from path2d.start, path2d.angle, and path2d.operations. turn, orient, push, and pop are not stored; forward is emitted as line_to so the replay does not depend on a lost heading.

Arguments:
  • path2d: Path to serialize.
  • n_round: Decimal places for coordinates and lengths derived from them. None uses runtime_defaults['n_round'].
Returns:

Python source that builds an equivalent Path2D.

Raises:
  • ValueError: If an operation subtype has no code mapping, or n_round is negative.
  • TypeError: If a style value cannot be serialized.
Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> sample = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=0).line_to((40, 0)).close()
>>> print(sg.path_code(sample))
path = sg.Path2D(start=(0, 0), angle=0)
path.line_to((40, 0))
path.close()
>>> messy = sg.Path2D((0, 0), angle=0).line_to((10.126, 0))
>>> print(sg.path_code(messy, n_round=2))
path = sg.Path2D(start=(0, 0), angle=0)
path.line_to((10.13, 0))
def svg_path_to_path2d(svg_path: str) -> Path2D: 
2537def svg_path_to_path2d(svg_path: str) -> Path2D:
2538    """Parse an SVG path ``d`` string into a ``Path2D``.
2539
2540        Args:
2541        svg_path: SVG path data string.
2542
2543        Returns:
2544        Path2D: Equivalent path.
2545
2546    Examples:
2547        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2548        >>> p = sg.svg_path_to_path2d("M 0 0 L 10 0 L 10 10 Z")
2549        >>> p.closed
2550        True
2551"""
2552    if not svg_path:
2553        return Path2D()
2554
2555    # Tokenizer
2556    tokens = re.findall(
2557        r"[A-Za-z]|[-+]?(?:\d*\.\d+|\d+)(?:[eE][-+]?\d+)?", svg_path
2558    )
2559
2560    start_point = (0.0, 0.0)
2561    idx = 0
2562
2563    # Handle optional start M strictly for initialization
2564    if idx < len(tokens) and tokens[idx].lower() == "m":
2565        try:
2566            x = float(tokens[idx + 1])
2567            y = float(tokens[idx + 2])
2568            start_point = (x, y)
2569            # We consume M x y by setting start
2570            # But we need to be careful if M has multiple points (implicit L)
2571            # or if we want to run the loop cleanly.
2572            # Easier: Just start at (0,0) and let the first Move set the pos.
2573            # But Path2D always starts with a point.
2574            # So initialization with correct start is better.
2575            idx = 3
2576        except IndexError:
2577            pass
2578
2579    lp = Path2D(start=start_point)
2580
2581    # If we consumed the first coordinate, we must handle implicit L if any.
2582    # The loop below handles commands.
2583    # If we skipped M x y, the next token might be a number (implicit L) or a Command.
2584    # We need to prime 'current_cmd' if we skipped.
2585
2586    current_cmd = ""
2587    i = 0
2588
2589    if idx == 3:
2590        i = 3
2591        # If the first command was 'm' (relative), and we treated it as absolute for start,
2592        # subsequent implicit linetos are relative.
2593        # If 'M', absolute.
2594        first_cmd = tokens[0]
2595        if first_cmd == "M":
2596            current_cmd = "L"
2597        if first_cmd == "m":
2598            current_cmd = "l"
2599
2600    while i < len(tokens):
2601        t = tokens[i]
2602
2603        if t.isalpha():
2604            current_cmd = t
2605            i += 1
2606        else:
2607            if not current_cmd:
2608                # Should not happen if path is valid
2609                i += 1
2610                continue
2611            # Implicit command logic
2612            # If M/m -> L/l
2613            if current_cmd == "M":
2614                current_cmd = "L"
2615            elif current_cmd == "m":
2616                current_cmd = "l"
2617            # L, l, H, h, V, v, C, c, S, s, Q, q, T, t, A, a remain same
2618
2619        cmd_lower = current_cmd.lower()
2620        is_rel = current_cmd == cmd_lower
2621
2622        if cmd_lower == "z":
2623            lp.close()
2624
2625        elif cmd_lower == "m":
2626            coords, i = _get_path_nums(tokens, i, 2)
2627            if coords:
2628                if is_rel:
2629                    lp.r_move(*coords)
2630                else:
2631                    lp.move_to(coords)
2632
2633        elif cmd_lower == "l":
2634            coords, i = _get_path_nums(tokens, i, 2)
2635            if coords:
2636                if is_rel:
2637                    lp.r_line(*coords)
2638                else:
2639                    lp.line_to(coords)
2640
2641        elif cmd_lower == "h":
2642            coords, i = _get_path_nums(tokens, i, 1)
2643            if coords:
2644                val = coords[0]
2645                if is_rel:
2646                    lp.r_h_line(val)
2647                else:
2648                    lp.h_line_to(val)
2649
2650        elif cmd_lower == "v":
2651            coords, i = _get_path_nums(tokens, i, 1)
2652            if coords:
2653                val = coords[0]
2654                if is_rel:
2655                    lp.r_v_line(val)
2656                else:
2657                    lp.v_line_to(val)
2658
2659        elif cmd_lower == "c":
2660            coords, i = _get_path_nums(tokens, i, 6)
2661            if coords:
2662                c1 = (coords[0], coords[1])
2663                c2 = (coords[2], coords[3])
2664                end = (coords[4], coords[5])
2665
2666                if is_rel:
2667                    cur_x, cur_y = lp.pos
2668                    c1 = (cur_x + c1[0], cur_y + c1[1])
2669                    c2 = (cur_x + c2[0], cur_y + c2[1])
2670                    end = (cur_x + end[0], cur_y + end[1])
2671
2672                lp.cubic_to(c1, c2, end)
2673
2674        elif cmd_lower == "s":
2675            coords, i = _get_path_nums(tokens, i, 4)
2676            if coords:
2677                c2 = (coords[0], coords[1])
2678                end = (coords[2], coords[3])
2679
2680                prev_c2 = lp.pos
2681                last_op = lp.operations[-1] if lp.operations else None
2682                # Check for Cubic/BlendCubic
2683                if last_op and last_op.subtype in _CUBIC_PATH_OPS:
2684                    # data: (start, c1, c2, end)
2685                    prev_c2 = last_op.data[2]
2686
2687                cur_x, cur_y = lp.pos
2688                ref_x = 2 * cur_x - prev_c2[0]
2689                ref_y = 2 * cur_y - prev_c2[1]
2690                c1 = (ref_x, ref_y)
2691
2692                if is_rel:
2693                    cur_x, cur_y = lp.pos
2694                    c2 = (cur_x + c2[0], cur_y + c2[1])
2695                    end = (cur_x + end[0], cur_y + end[1])
2696
2697                lp.cubic_to(c1, c2, end)
2698
2699        elif cmd_lower == "q":
2700            coords, i = _get_path_nums(tokens, i, 4)
2701            if coords:
2702                c1 = (coords[0], coords[1])
2703                end = (coords[2], coords[3])
2704                if is_rel:
2705                    cur_x, cur_y = lp.pos
2706                    c1 = (cur_x + c1[0], cur_y + c1[1])
2707                    end = (cur_x + end[0], cur_y + end[1])
2708                lp.quad_to(c1, end)
2709
2710        elif cmd_lower == "t":
2711            coords, i = _get_path_nums(tokens, i, 2)
2712            if coords:
2713                end = (coords[0], coords[1])
2714
2715                prev_c1 = lp.pos
2716                last_op = lp.operations[-1] if lp.operations else None
2717                if last_op and last_op.subtype in _QUAD_PATH_OPS:
2718                    # data: (start, c1, end) or similar?
2719                    # quad_to adds: PathOps.QUAD_TO, (pos, c1, end)
2720                    prev_c1 = last_op.data[1]
2721
2722                cur_x, cur_y = lp.pos
2723                ref_x = 2 * cur_x - prev_c1[0]
2724                ref_y = 2 * cur_y - prev_c1[1]
2725                c1 = (ref_x, ref_y)
2726
2727                if is_rel:
2728                    end = (cur_x + end[0], cur_y + end[1])
2729
2730                lp.quad_to(c1, end)
2731
2732        elif cmd_lower == "a":
2733            coords, i = _get_path_nums(tokens, i, 7)
2734            if coords:
2735                rx, ry = coords[0], coords[1]
2736                rot_deg = coords[2]
2737                large_arc = bool(coords[3])
2738                sweep = bool(coords[4])
2739                end = (coords[5], coords[6])
2740
2741                if is_rel:
2742                    cur_x, cur_y = lp.pos
2743                    end = (cur_x + end[0], cur_y + end[1])
2744
2745                params = _get_svg_arc_params(
2746                    lp.pos, rx, ry, rot_deg, large_arc, sweep, end
2747                )
2748
2749                if params is not None and params[0] is PathOps.LINE_TO:
2750                    lp.line_to(params[1])
2751                elif params is not None and params[0] is PathOps.ARC:
2752                    (
2753                        _op,
2754                        radius_x,
2755                        radius_y,
2756                        start_angle,
2757                        span_angle,
2758                        rot_angle,
2759                    ) = params
2760                    signed_span = span_angle
2761                    lp.arc(
2762                        radius_x,
2763                        radius_y,
2764                        start_angle,
2765                        abs(signed_span),
2766                        rot_angle=rot_angle,
2767                        clockwise=signed_span < 0,
2768                    )
2769
2770    return lp

Parse an SVG path d string into a Path2D.

Args:
svg_path: SVG path data string.

Returns:
Path2D: Equivalent path.
Examples:

def shape_to_path2d( shape: simetri.shapes.shape.Shape, *, turns: bool = False, relative: bool = False) -> Path2D: 
2898def shape_to_path2d(
2899    shape: Shape,
2900    *,
2901    turns: bool = False,
2902    relative: bool = False,
2903) -> Path2D:
2904    """Convert a ``Shape`` into an equivalent ``Path2D``.
2905
2906    By default the pen ``move_to``s the first vertex, ``line_to``s each
2907    remaining vertex, and ``close()`` when the shape is closed.
2908
2909    With ``turns=True``, the pen starts at the first vertex (no initial
2910    ``move_to``) and each edge is recorded as ``turn(angle, distance)``.
2911
2912    With ``relative=True`` and ``turns=False``, axis-aligned edges use
2913    ``r_h_line`` / ``r_v_line``; other edges use ``r_line``.
2914
2915    Args:
2916        shape: Source shape.
2917        turns: Use turtle-style ``turn`` / ``forward`` for edges.
2918        relative: Use relative line ops when ``turns`` is False.
2919
2920    Returns:
2921        Path2D: Path following the shape vertices.
2922
2923    Examples:
2924        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2925        >>> from simetri.base.all_enums import PathOperation as PO
2926        >>> from simetri.geom.nonlinear.path import shape_to_path2d
2927        >>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40)], closed=True)
2928        >>> shape_to_path2d(rect).closed
2929        True
2930        >>> any(op.subtype == PO.FORWARD for op in shape_to_path2d(rect, turns=True).operations)
2931        True
2932        >>> ops = {op.subtype for op in shape_to_path2d(rect, relative=True).operations}
2933        >>> PO.R_H_LINE in ops and PO.R_V_LINE in ops
2934        True
2935"""
2936    vertices = shape.vertices
2937    if not vertices:
2938        return Path2D()
2939
2940    if turns:
2941        path = Path2D(vertices[0])
2942        start = vertices[0]
2943        for vert in vertices[1:]:
2944            _shape_edge_turn(path, start, vert)
2945            start = vert
2946        if shape.closed:
2947            path.close()
2948        return path
2949
2950    path = Path2D()
2951    path.move_to(vertices[0])
2952    start = vertices[0]
2953    for vert in vertices[1:]:
2954        if relative:
2955            _shape_edge_relative(path, start, vert)
2956        else:
2957            path.line_to(vert)
2958        start = vert
2959    if shape.closed:
2960        path.close()
2961    return path

Convert a Shape into an equivalent Path2D.

By default the pen move_tos the first vertex, line_tos each remaining vertex, and close() when the shape is closed.

With turns=True, the pen starts at the first vertex (no initial move_to) and each edge is recorded as turn(angle, distance).

With relative=True and turns=False, axis-aligned edges use r_h_line / r_v_line; other edges use r_line.

Arguments:
  • shape: Source shape.
  • turns: Use turtle-style turn / forward for edges.
  • relative: Use relative line ops when turns is False.
Returns:

Path2D: Path following the shape vertices.

Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> from simetri.base.all_enums import PathOperation as PO
>>> from simetri.geom.nonlinear.path import shape_to_path2d
>>> rect = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40)], closed=True)
>>> shape_to_path2d(rect).closed
True
>>> any(op.subtype == PO.FORWARD for op in shape_to_path2d(rect, turns=True).operations)
True
>>> ops = {op.subtype for op in shape_to_path2d(rect, relative=True).operations}
>>> PO.R_H_LINE in ops and PO.R_V_LINE in ops
True
def shape_to_path( shape: simetri.shapes.shape.Shape, *, turns: bool = False, relative: bool = False) -> Path2D:

2965    shape: Shape,
2966    *,

2969) -> Path2D:
2970    """Convert a ``Shape`` into a ``Path2D`` (alias of ``shape_to_path2d``).

2980    Examples:

def group_to_path(group: simetri.group.batch.Group) -> Path2D: 
2990def group_to_path(group: Group) -> Path2D:
2991    """Convert a ``Group`` of shapes into a single ``Path2D``.
2992
2993    Args:
2994    group: Source group.
2995
2996    Returns:
2997    Path2D: Path that visits each shape as a subpath.
2998
2999    Examples:
3000        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
3001        >>> from simetri.geom.nonlinear.path import group_to_path
3002        >>> g = sg.Group([sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0)]), sg.Shape([(80, 0), (60, 0)])])
3003        >>> p = group_to_path(g)
3004        >>> [op.subtype.name for op in p.operations]
3005        ['MOVE_TO', 'LINE_TO', 'MOVE_TO', 'LINE_TO']
3006        >>> [[round(c, 6) for c in q[:2]] for q in p.vertices]
3007        [[0.0, 0.0], [40.0, 0.0], [80.0, 0.0], [60.0, 0.0]]
3008"""
3009    shapes = group.all_shapes
3010    path = Path2D()
3011    path.move_to(shapes[0][0])
3012    for i, shape in enumerate(shapes):
3013        if i > 0:
3014            path.move_to(shape[0])
3015        for vert in shape.vertices[1:]:
3016            path.line_to(vert)
3017        if shape.closed:
3018            path.line_to(shape[0])
3019
3020    return path

def group_to_nonzero_path(group: simetri.group.batch.Group) -> Path2D: 
3023def group_to_nonzero_path(group: Group) -> Path2D:
3024    """Build one ``Path2D`` from a group's shapes for non-zero compound fill.
3025
3026    The largest-area closed contour keeps its vertex order; every other
3027    closed contour is reversed so it counts as a hole under the non-zero rule.
3028
3029    Args:
3030        group: Source group.
3031
3032    Returns:
3033        Path2D: Combined subpaths with ``fill_mode`` ``NONZERO``.
3034
3035    Raises:
3036        ValueError: If the group has no shape geometry.
3037
3038    Examples:
3039        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
3040        >>> from simetri.geom.nonlinear.path import group_to_nonzero_path
3041        >>> outer = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (80, 0), (80, 80), (0, 80)], closed=True)
3042        >>> inner = sg.Shape([(40, 40), (60, 40), (60, 60), (40, 60)], closed=True)
3043        >>> path = group_to_nonzero_path(sg.Group([outer, inner]))
3044        >>> path.fill_mode.name
3045        'NONZERO'
3046        >>> path.pos
3047        (40.0, 40.0)
3048    """
3049    shapes = group.all_shapes
3050    if not shapes:
3051        raise ValueError("group_to_nonzero_path requires at least one shape.")
3052    abs_areas = [abs(polygon_area(shape.vertices)) for shape in shapes]
3053    outer_index = abs_areas.index(max(abs_areas))
3054
3055    def ring_vertices(shape_index: int) -> list[PointType]:
3056        shape = shapes[shape_index]
3057        vertices = list(shape.vertices)
3058        if shape.closed and shape_index != outer_index:
3059            vertices = list(reversed(vertices))
3060        return vertices
3061
3062    first_ring = ring_vertices(0)
3063    path = Path2D(start=first_ring[0], fill_mode=FillMode.NONZERO)
3064    for vertex in first_ring[1:]:
3065        path.line_to(vertex)
3066    if shapes[0].closed:
3067        path.close()
3068    for shape_index in range(1, len(shapes)):
3069        ring = ring_vertices(shape_index)
3070        path.move_to(ring[0])
3071        for vertex in ring[1:]:
3072            path.line_to(vertex)
3073        if shapes[shape_index].closed:
3074            path.close()
3075    return path

Build one Path2D from a group's shapes for non-zero compound fill.

The largest-area closed contour keeps its vertex order; every other closed contour is reversed so it counts as a hole under the non-zero rule.

Arguments:
  • group: Source group.
Returns:

Path2D: Combined subpaths with fill_mode NONZERO.

Raises:
  • ValueError: If the group has no shape geometry.
Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> from simetri.geom.nonlinear.path import group_to_nonzero_path
>>> outer = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (80, 0), (80, 80), (0, 80)], closed=True)
>>> inner = sg.Shape([(40, 40), (60, 40), (60, 60), (40, 60)], closed=True)
>>> path = group_to_nonzero_path(sg.Group([outer, inner]))
>>> path.fill_mode.name
'NONZERO'
>>> path.pos
(40.0, 40.0)
